1.1: All wisdom comes from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and is with Him forever.
1.2:
Who may number the sand of the sea and the drops of rain, 
And the days of eternity?
1.3:
Who may search out the height of the shamayim, 
And the breadth of the earth, and the deep, and wisdom?
1.4:
Wisdom has been created before all, 
And the understanding of insight from everlasting.
1.5:
The Word of Elohim Most High is the fountain of wisdom; 
And her ways are everlasting Commands.
1.6:
To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? 
Or who has known her wise counsels?
1.7:
Unto whom has the knowledge of wisdom been made manifest? 
And who has understood her great experience?
1.8:
There is One wise and greatly to be revered: 
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sitting upon His throne.
1.9:
He created her, and saw her, and measured her, 
And poured her out upon all His works.
1.10:
She is with all flesh according to His gift, 
And He has given her to those who love Him.
1.11:
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is esteem and splendor and gladness, 
And a crown of rejoicing.
1.12:
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 makes a glad heart, 
And gives joy, and gladness, and a long life.
1.13:
It shall go well to the end for he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And he shall receive beraḵah in the day of his death.
1.14:
To revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the beginning of wisdom: 
And it was created with the trustworthy in the womb.
1.15:
She has built an everlasting foundation with men, 
And she shall continue with their seed.
1.16:
To revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is fullness of wisdom, 
And fills men with her fruits.
1.17:
She fills all their house with that which is desirable, 
And the gatherers with her increase.
1.19:
Wisdom rains down skill and knowledge of understanding, 
And exalts to esteem those who hold her fast.
1.20:
The root of wisdom is to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And the branches thereof are long life.
1.21:
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 drives away sins, 
And where it is present, it turns away wrath.
1.22:
A wrathful man cannot be declared right; 
For the sway of his wrath shall be his destruction.
1.23:
A patient man shall weep for a time, 
And afterward joy shall spring up in him.
1.24:
He shall hold his words for a time, 
And the lips of many shall declare his wisdom.
1.25:
The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisdom: 
But reverence is an abomination to a sinner.
1.26:
If you desire wisdom, guard the Commands, 
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall give her to you.
1.27:
For the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is wisdom and instruction; 
And belief and meekness are his delight.
1.28:
Do not doubt the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 when you are poor: 
And do not come to him with a double mind.
1.29:
Do not be a hypocrite in the sight of men, 
And take heed what you speak.
1.30:
Do not exalt yourself, lest you fall, and bring shame upon yourself, 
And so Elohim uncover your secrets, and throw you down in the midst of the assembly, 
Because you did not come in truth to the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
But your heart is full of deceit.

10.1:
A wise judge shall instruct his people; 
And the reign of a clever man is well ordered.
10.3:
An unwise meleḵ destroys his people; 
But through the insight of those who are in authority the city shall be inhabited.
10.4:
The power of the earth is in the hand 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And in due time He shall appoint it to One who is worthy.
10.5:
The prosperity of man is in the hand of Elohim; 
And He shall lay His esteem upon the face of the scribe.
10.6:
Do not bear hatred against your neighbor for every wrong; 
And do not act as an insulter at all.
10.7:
Pride is hateful before Elohim and man; 
And against both, one commits wickedness.
10.8:
Because of unrighteous dealings, maltreatment, and wealth gained by deceit, 
The rule is transferred from one people to another.
10.10:
The physician ends a long disease; 
And he who is a meleḵ today shall die tomorrow.
10.11:
For when a man is dead, 
He shall inherit insects, creatures and worms.
10.12:
The beginning of pride is when one departs from Elohim, 
And his heart is turned away from his Maker.
10.13:
For pride is the beginning of sin, 
And he who has it shall pour out abominations: 
And therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brings upon them unknown calamity, 
And overthrows them completely.
10.14:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has thrown down the thrones of proud princes, 
And appointed the meek in their place.
10.15:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has plucked up the roots of the proud nations, 
And planted the lowly in their place.
10.16:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 overthrew the lands of the gentiles, 
And destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
10.17:
He took some of them away, and destroyed them, 
And has caused their remembrance to cease from the earth.
10.18:
Pride was not made for man, 
Nor violent wrath for those who are born of a woman.
10.19:
Those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are a continual seed, 
And those who love Him an esteemed plant. 
Those who disregard the Law are a shameful seed; 
Those who transgress the Commands are a deceptive seed.
10.20:
Among brothers he who is chief is esteemed; 
So are those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in His eyes.
10.21:
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 goes before the obtaining of authority; 
But stubbornness and pride is the loss of it.
10.22:
Whether he is wealthy, noble or poor, 
Their esteem is the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
10.23:
It is not right to despise the poor who has understanding; 
Neither is it proper to exalt a sinner.
10.24:
Great men and judges and rulers shall be esteemed; 
Yet there is none greater than he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
10.25:
Those who are free shall do service to the servant that is wise; 
And he who has knowledge shall not grumble when he is instructed.
10.26:
Do not be overwise in doing your business; 
And do not boast in the time of your distress.
10.27:
Better is he who labors and overflows in all, 
Than he who boasts and lacks bread.
10.28:
My son, esteem your being in meekness, 
And give it respect according to its quality.
10.29:
Who shall declare right he who sins against his own being? 
And who shall esteem he who shames his own life?
10.30:
The poor man is esteemed for his skill, 
And the wealthy man is esteemed for his wealth.
10.31:
He who is esteemed in poverty, how much more in wealth? 
And he who is ashamed in wealth, how much more in poverty?

11.1:
Wisdom lifts up the head of he who is of low degree, 
And makes him to sit among great men.
11.2:
Do not commend a man for his good looks; 
Neither despise a man for his outward appearance.
11.3:
The bee is little among those that fly; 
But her fruit is the first of that which is sweet.
11.4:
Do not boast of your garments and clothes, 
And do not exalt yourself in the day of esteem; 
For the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are wondrous, 
And His works among men are hidden.
11.5:
Many melaḵim have sat down on the ground; 
And one that was never considered has worn the crown.
11.6:
Many mighty men have been greatly shamed; 
And those esteemed delivered into other men’s hands.
11.7:
Do not accuse before you have examined the truth; 
Understand first, and then reprove.
11.8:
Do not answer before you have heard the case; 
Neither interrupt men in the middle of speaking.
11.9:
Do not strive in a matter that does not concern you; 
And do not sit in judgment with sinners.
11.11:
There is one who labors, and struggles, and hurries, 
And is so much more behind.
11.12:
Again, there is another that is slow, and needs help, 
Lacking skill, and full of poverty; 
Yet the eye of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looks upon him for good, 
And raises him up from his humiliation,
11.13:
And lifts his head from misery; 
So that many see His peace over all this.
11.14:
Prosperity and adversity, life and death, 
Poverty and wealth, come from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
11.15:
Wisdom, knowledge and understanding of the Law, are of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; 
Love, and the way of good works, are from Him.
11.16:
Sin and darkness had their beginning together with sinners; 
And evil shall grow old with those who boast in them.
11.17:
The gift of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 remains with the righteous, 
And His favor brings peace forever.
11.18:
There is he who grows wealthy by his cunning and frugality, 
And this is the portion of his reward:
11.19:
For he says, “I have found rest, and now shall eat continually of my goods.” 
And yet he does not know what event shall come upon him, 
And that he must leave those to others, and die.
11.20:
Be steadfast in your agreement, and be acquainted with it, 
And grow old in your work.
11.22:
The beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is in the reward of the reverent, 
And suddenly He makes his beraḵah flourish.
11.23:
Do not say, “What profit is there of my service? 
And what good shall I have afterward?”
11.24:
Again, do not say, “I have enough, and possess much, 
And what evil shall come to me afterward?”
11.25:
In the day of good there is a forgetfulness of affliction; 
And in the day of affliction there is no remembrance of good.
11.26: For it is light for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to reward a man according to his ways on the day of death.
11.27:
The affliction of an hour makes a man forget pleasure; 
And in the end his deeds shall be exposed.
11.28:
Judge none happy before his death; 
For a man shall be known in his children.
11.29:
Do not bring every man into your house; 
For the deceitful man has many schemes.
11.31:
For he lies in wait, and turns good into evil, 
And in that which is worthy of praise shall accuse you.
11.32:
From a spark of fire a heap of coals is kindled: 
And a sinful man lays in wait for blood.
11.33:
Take heed of an evil-doer, for he works wickedness; 
Lest he bring upon you an everlasting stain.
11.34:
Receive a stranger into your house, and he shall disturb you, 
And turn you out of your own.

12.1:
When you do good, know to whom you do it; 
So you shall be thanked for your good works.
12.2:
Do good to the upright, and you shall find a recompense; 
And if not from him, even from the Most High.
12.3:
No good shall come to he who is always occupied with evil, 
Nor to he who does no kind deed.
12.4: Give to the upright man, and do not help a sinner.
12.6:
For the Most High hates sinners, and shall repay the wicked with retribution, 
And keeps them for the great day of their punishment.
12.7: Give to the good, and do not help the sinner.
12.8:
A friend cannot be known in good times; 
And an enemy cannot be hidden in adversity.
12.9:
In the prosperity of a man enemies shall be grieved: 
But in his adversity even a friend shall turn away.
12.10:
Never trust your enemy; 
For as iron rusts, so is his wickedness.
12.11:
Though he humbles himself, and comes bowed down, 
Yet be on your guard and beware of him, 
And be to him as if you had wiped a mirror, 
And you shall know that its tarnish has not been wiped away altogether.
12.12:
Do not put him near you, 
Lest when he has overthrown you, he stands in your place; 
Neither let him sit at your right hand, 
Lest he seek to take your seat, and you remember my words in the end, 
And be pierced by them.
12.13:
Who shall pity a charmer that is bitten by a serpent, 
Or any who come near wild beasts?
12.14:
So one that goes to a sinner, and is defiled by him in his sins, 
Who shall pity?
12.15:
For a while he shall remain with you, 
But if you begin to fall, he shall not wait.
12.16:
An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, 
But in his heart he imagines how to throw you into a pit; 
He weeps with his eyes, but if he finds opportunity, 
He shall not be satisfied with blood.
12.17:
If adversity comes upon you, you shall find him there first; 
And though he pretends to help you, even so he shall wrong you.
12.18:
He shall shake his head, and clap his hands, 
And whisper much, and change his face.

13.1:
He who handles tar is made unclean by it; 
And he who has fellowship with a proud man shall be like him.
13.3:
The wealthy man has done wrong, and yet he threatens all; 
The poor is wronged, and he must also plead.
13.4:
If you profit him, he shall use you; 
But if you have naught, he shall forsake you.
13.5:
If you possess whatever, he shall live with you; 
He shall also leave you naked, and shall not be sorry for it.
13.7:
And he shall shame you with his delicacies, 
Until he has drained you dry two or three times, 
And in the end he shall mock you afterward. 
When he sees you, he shall forsake you, and shake his head at you.
13.8: Beware that you are not deceived and brought down in your rejoicing.
13.9:
If you are invited by a mighty man, withdraw yourself, 
And he shall invite you so much more.
13.10:
Do not push yourself on him, lest you be turned away; 
Do not stand far off, lest you be forgotten.
13.12:
But cruelly he shall lay up your words, and not spare to do you harm, 
And deliver you up.
13.14:
Love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all your life, 
And call upon Him for your deliverance.
13.15:
Every beast loves its kind, 
And every man loves his neighbor.
13.16:
All flesh associates according to kind, 
And a man shall cling to those like himself.
13.17:
What fellowship has the wolf with the lamb? 
So the sinner with the righteous.
13.18:
What agreement is there between the hyena and a dog? 
And what peace between the wealthy and the poor?
13.19:
As the wild donkey is the lion’s prey in the wilderness; 
So the wealthy eat up the poor.
13.20:
As the proud hate humility; 
So does the wealthy abhor the poor.
13.21:
A wealthy man beginning to fall is supported by his friends; 
But a poor man fallen is pushed away by his friends.
13.23:
When a wealthy man speaks, every man holds his tongue, 
And look, what he says, they exalt it to the clouds; 
But if the poor man speaks, they say, “What fellow is this?” 
And if he stumbles, they shall help to overthrow him.
13.24:
Wealth is good to he who has no sin, 
And poverty is evil in the mouth of the wicked.
13.25:
The heart of a man changes his face, whether it be for good or evil; 
And a glad heart makes a good face.
13.26:
A good face is a sign of a heart that is good; 
And the searching out of parables is a wearisome labor of the mind.

14.1:
Ashrĕ is the man that has not slipped with his mouth, 
And is not pierced with the great number of sins.
14.2:
Ashrĕ is he whose conscience has not condemned him, 
And who has not fallen from his expectancy in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.3:
Wealth is not fitting for a miser; 
And what should an envious man do with silver?
14.4:
He who gathers by depriving his own being, 
Gathers for others that shall spend his goods loosely.
14.5:
He who is evil to himself, to whom shall he be good? 
He shall not take pleasure in his goods.
14.6:
There is none worse than he who envies himself; 
And this is to repay for his wickedness.
14.7:
And if he does good, he does it unwillingly; 
And in the end he shall declare his wickedness.
14.8:
The greedy man has an evil eye; 
He turns away his face, and despises men.
14.9:
A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion; 
And the wickedness of the wicked dries up his being.
14.10:
A wicked eye is greedy for bread, 
And he is a miser at his table.
14.11:
My son, according to your ability do good to yourself, 
And give 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 His due offering.
14.12:
Remember that death shall not be long in coming, 
And that the promise of the grave is not revealed to you.
14.13:
Do good to your friend before you die, 
And according to your ability stretch out your hand and give to him.
14.14:
Do not deprive yourself of a good day, 
And do not let the share of a good desire overlook you.
14.15:
Shall you not leave your hardships to another? 
And your labors to be divided by lot?
14.16:
Give and take, and qadosh your being; 
For there is no seeking delicacies in the grave.
14.19:
Every work rots and eats away, 
And the worker of it shall go likewise.
14.20:
Ashrĕ is the man who meditates on goodness in wisdom, 
And thinks upon qodesh matters with his understanding.
14.21:
He who considers her ways in his heart, 
Shall also have understanding of her secrets.
14.22: Go after her as one that follows, and lie in wait on her ways.
14.23: He who peers in her windows shall also listen at her doors.
14.24: He who lodges near her house shall also fasten a peg on her walls.
14.25:
He shall pitch his tent near to her, 
And shall lodge in a lodging where goodness is.
14.26:
He shall put his children under her shelter, 
And shall lodge under her branches.
14.27:
By her he shall be covered from heat, 
And in her esteem he shall dwell.

15.1:
He who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall do good, 
And he who has the knowledge of the Law shall obtain her.
15.2:
And as a mother she shall meet him, 
And receive him as a wife married in maidenhood.
15.3:
With the bread of understanding she shall feed him, 
And give him the water of wisdom to drink.
15.4:
He shall be visited by her, and shall not be moved; 
And shall rely on her, and shall not be ashamed.
15.5:
She shall exalt him above his neighbors, 
And she shall open his mouth in the midst of the assembly.
15.6:
He shall find joy and a crown of gladness, 
And she shall cause him to inherit an everlasting name.
15.7:
But foolish men shall not obtain her, 
And sinners shall not see her.
15.8:
For she is far from pride, 
And men that are liars cannot remember her.
15.9:
Praise is not fitting for the mouth of a sinner, 
For it was not sent to him by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.10:
For praise shall be uttered in wisdom, 
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall make it prosper.
15.11:
Do not say, “It is because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that I fell away.” 
For you ought not to do that which He hates.
15.12:
Do not say, “He has caused me to stray.” 
For He has no need of the sinful man.
15.13:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hates all abomination; 
And those who revere Elohim do not love it.
15.14:
He Himself made man from the beginning, 
And left him in the hand of his own counsel;
15.15:
So you shall guard the Commands, 
And act trustworthily.
15.16:
He has put fire and water before you; 
Stretch out your hand to which you choose.
15.17:
Ḥai and death is before man; 
And what he chooses shall be given him.
15.18:
For the wisdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is great, 
And He is mighty in power, and sees all.
15.19:
And His eyes are upon those who revere Him, 
And He knows every work of man.
15.20:
He has commanded no man to do wickedly, 
Neither has He given any man permission to sin.

16.1:
Do not desire a great number of worthless children, 
Neither delight in wicked sons.
16.2:
Though they increase, do not rejoice in them, 
Unless the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with them.
16.4:
For by one that has understanding the city shall be filled; 
But the offspring of the wicked shall be quickly laid waste.
16.5:
Many such matters I have seen with my eyes, 
And my ear has heard greater than these.
16.6:
In the assembly of the wicked a fire shall be kindled; 
And in a rebellious nation wrath is lit on fire.
16.7:
He was not appeased toward the giants of old, 
Who fell in the strength of their foolishness.
16.8:
Neither did He spare the place where Lot sojourned, 
But loathed them for their pride.
16.9:
He had no compassion for the people of destruction, 
Who were taken away in their sins;
16.10:
Nor the six hundred thousand foot soldiers, 
Who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.
16.11:
And if there is one stiff-necked among the people, 
It is marvel if he escapes unpunished; 
For kindness and wrath are with Him. 
He is mighty to forgive, and to pour out displeasure.
16.12:
As His kindness is great, so is His discipline also. 
He judges a man according to his works.
16.13:
The sinner shall not escape with his plunder; 
And the patience of the righteous shall not be defeated.
16.14:
Make room for every act of kindness; 
For everyone shall receive according to his works.
16.15:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know Him, 
That His mighty works might be known to the world.
16.16:
His kindness is revealed to every creature; 
And He has separated His light from the darkness and is unbreakable.
16.17:
Do not say, "I shall hide myself from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. 
Shall any remember me from above? 
I shall not be remembered among so many people; 
For what is my being among such a limitless number of creatures?"
16.18:
See, the shamayim, and the shamayim of shamayim, 
The deep, and the earth, and all that is in it, 
Shall be moved at His visitation.
16.19:
The mountains and foundations of the earth shall also be shaken with trembling, 
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looks upon them.
16.20:
No heart may think upon these worthily; 
And who is able to perceive His ways?
16.21:
It is a whirlwind that no man sees; 
For most of his works are hidden.
16.22:
Who shall declare the works of His righteousness? 
Or who shall endure them? 
For His decree is far off, 
And the trial of all is at the end.
16.23:
He who lacks understanding shall think upon emptiness; 
And a foolish man straying plots foolishness.
16.24:
My son, listen to me and learn knowledge, 
And know my words in your heart.
16.25:
I shall present instruction by measure, 
And declare His knowledge exactly.
16.26:
The works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are done in right-ruling from the beginning; 
And from the time He made them He laid out their parts.
16.28:
None of them withholds another, 
And they never disobey His word.
16.29:
After this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looked upon the earth, 
And filled it with His good things.
16.30:
Has He covered the face of it with all manner of living creatures; 
And they shall return to it again.

17.1:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 created man from the earth, 
And returns him to it again.
17.2:
He gave them few days, and a short time, 
And also authority over that within it.
17.3:
He gave them strength within themselves, 
And made them according to His image,
17.4:
And put the fear of man upon all flesh, 
And gave him rule over beasts and birds.
17.5:
They received the use of the five senses of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And in the sixth place He gave them understanding, 
And in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the thoughts.
17.6:
Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, 
He gave them to understand.
17.7:
He filled them with the knowledge of understanding, 
And showed them good and evil.
17.8:
He put His eye on their hearts, 
That He might show them the greatness of His works.
17.9:
He appointed them to boast in His marvelous deeds forever, 
That they might declare His works with understanding.
17.10: And the elect shall praise His qodesh Name.
17.11:
Besides this He gave them knowledge, 
And the Law of Ḥai for an inheritance.
17.12:
He made an everlasting Covenant with them, 
And gave them His Right-Rulings.
17.13:
Their eyes saw the excellence of His esteem, 
And their ears heard His esteemed voice.
17.14:
And He said to them, “Beware of all unrighteousness.” 
And He gave every man Command concerning his neighbor.
17.15:
Their ways are ever before Him, 
And shall not be hid from His eyes.
17.16:
Every man from his youth is given to evil; 
Neither could they make hearts of flesh for themselves from stony.
17.17:
For in the division of the nations of the whole earth He appointed a ruler over every people; 
But Yisra’ĕl is the portion of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
17.18:
Whom being His first-born, He nourishes with discipline, 
And giving him the light of His love, does not forsake him.
17.19:
Therefore all their works are as the sun before Him, 
And His eyes are continually upon their ways.
17.20:
None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from Him, 
But all their sins are before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.21:
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 showing favor and knowing His workmanship, 
Neither left nor forsook them, but spared them.
17.22:
The kind deeds of a man are as a signet with Him, 
And He shall guard the good deeds of man as the apple of His eye, 
And give repentance to His sons and daughters.
17.23:
Afterwards He shall rise up and reward them, 
And render their recompense upon their heads.
17.24:
And to those who repent, He provides a return, 
And comforts those whose expectancy is failing.
17.25:
Return to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and leave your sins. 
Make your prayer before His face, and be guiltless.
17.27:
Who shall praise the Most High in the grave, 
Except for those who live and give thanks?
17.28:
Thanksgiving perishes from the dead, as from one who is not; 
The living and perfect in heart shall praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
17.29:
How great is the kindness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, 
And His compassion to those who turn to Him in qodeshah!
17.30:
For not all is within man, 
For the son of man is not incorruptible.
17.31:
What is brighter than the sun, yet its light fails? 
So flesh and blood shall imagine evil.
17.32:
He views the power of the height of the shamayim; 
And all men are but dust and ashes.

18.1: He who lives forever has created all in its entirety.
18.2:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 alone is righteous, 
And there is no other but He,
18.3:
Who guides the world with the palm of His hand, 
And all obey His desire; 
For He is the Meleḵ of all by His power, 
Dividing the qodesh from among the profane.
18.4:
To whom has He given power to declare His works? 
And who shall find out His noble acts?
18.5:
Who shall measure the strength of His excellence? 
And who also shall tell of His kindnesses?
18.6:
As for the wondrous works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, there is naught taken from them, 
Nor any that are compared to them, 
Nor may the expanse of them be found out.
18.7:
When a man is finished, then one begins; 
And when he leaves, then he shall be uncertain.
18.8:
What is man, and what use is he? 
What is his good, and what is his evil?
18.9: The number of a man’s days at the greatest are a hundred years.
18.10:
As a drop of water into the sea, and a grain compared to the sand; 
So are a thousand years to everlasting days.
18.11:
Therefore Elohim is patient with them, 
And pours out His kindness upon them.
18.12:
He looked and saw their end to be evil; 
Therefore He multiplied His compassion.
18.14:
He has kindness on those who receive discipline, 
And who diligently seek after His Right-Rulings.
18.15:
My son, do not blemish your good deeds, 
Nor use harsh words when you give.
18.16:
Does the dew not relieve the heat? 
So a word is better than a gift.
18.17:
Look, is a word not better than a gift? 
But both are with one showing kindness.
18.18:
A fool shall reproach harshly, 
And a gift of the selfish consumes the eyes.
18.19:
Learn before you speak, 
And use healing if you are ever sick.
18.20:
Before judgment examine yourself, 
And in the day of visitation you shall find kindness.
18.21:
Humble yourself before you become sick, 
And in the time of sins show repentance.
18.22:
Let naught hinder you to pay your vow in due time, 
And do not delay till death to be declared right.
18.23:
Before you pray, prepare yourself; 
And do not be as one that tries 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
18.24:
Think upon the wrath that shall be in the end, 
And the time of vengeance, when He turns away His face.
18.25:
When you have enough, remember the time of hunger: 
And when you are wealthy, think upon poverty and need.
18.26:
From the morning until the evening the times change, 
And all are soon done before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
18.27:
A wise man shall revere in every matter, 
And in the day of sinning he shall beware of trespass. 
But a fool does not observe time.
18.28:
Every man of understanding knows wisdom, 
And shall praise he who finds her.
18.29:
Those who have understanding in words also become wise themselves, 
And pour forth splendid parables.
18.30:
Do not pursue your lusts, 
But restrain yourself from your appetites.
18.31:
If you give your being the desires that it pleases, 
It shall make you a mockery to your enemies that slander you.
18.32:
Do not revel in excessive pleasure, 
Nor be bound by its expense.

19.1:
A laborer that is given to drunkenness shall not be wealthy; 
And he who despises small matters shall fall little by little.
19.2:
Wine and women shall cause men of understanding to fall away: 
And he who clings to whores shall become hardened.
19.3:
Moths and worms shall have him to inherit, 
And a bold man shall be taken away.
19.4:
He who is hasty to give credit is light-minded; 
And he who sins corrupts his own being.
19.5:
Whoever takes pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: 
But he who resists pleasures crowns his ḥai.
19.6:
He who rules his tongue shall live without strife; 
And he who hates gossip shall have less evil.
19.7:
Do not repeat to another that which is told to you, 
And you shall not suffer harm.
19.8:
Whether to friend or enemy, do not speak of another’s life; 
And if you may without offense, do not reveal them.
19.9:
For if he hears and sees you, 
So in time to come he shall hate you.
19.10:
If you have heard a word, let it die with you; 
And be brave, it shall not burst you!
19.11:
A fool struggles with a word, 
As a woman in labor with a child.
19.12:
As an arrow that sticks in a man’s thigh, 
So is a word inside a fool.
19.13:
Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it; 
And if he has done it, that he does it no more.
19.14:
Admonish your friend, it may be he has not said it; 
And if he has, that he does not speak it again.
19.15:
Admonish a friend, for many times it is slander, 
And do not believe every whisper.
19.16:
There is one that slips in his speech, but not from his heart; 
And who is he who has not offended with his tongue?
19.17:
Admonish your neighbor before you threaten him; 
And not being wroth, give place to the Law of the Most High.
19.18:
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the beginning of acceptance, 
And wisdom obtains His love.
19.19:
The knowledge of the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the instruction of Ḥai: 
And those who do that which pleases Him, 
Shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.
19.21:
If a servant says to his master, “I shall not do as it pleases you.” 
Though afterward he does it, he angers him who feeds him.
19.22:
The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, 
Nor at any time is insight the counsel of sinners.
19.23:
There is a wickedness, and such is an abomination; 
And there is a fool lacking in wisdom.
19.24:
He who has little understanding, and reveres Elohim, 
Is better than one that has much wisdom, 
And transgresses the Law of the Most High.
19.26:
There is a wicked man that bows his head sadly; 
But inwardly he is full of deceit,
19.27:
Casting down his face, and making as if he did not hear. 
Where he is unknown, he shall do you evil before you are aware.
19.28:
And if for need of power he may cease from sinning, 
Yet when he finds opportunity he shall do evil.
19.29:
A man may be known by his appearance, 
And one that has understanding, by his face when you meet him.
19.30: A man’s dress, and excessive laughter, and walk, reveal what is.

2.1:
My son, if you come to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Prepare your being for trial.
2.2:
Prepare your heart, and constantly endure, 
And do not hasten in time of trouble.
2.3:
Cling to Him, and do not depart, 
That you may be increased at your latter end.
2.4:
Whatsoever is brought upon you, accept cheerfully, 
And be patient when you are brought low.
2.5:
For gold is tried in the fire, 
And acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
2.6:
Believe in Him, and He shall help you; 
Establish your way, and trust in Him.
2.7:
You who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, wait for His kindness; 
And do not turn aside, lest you fall.
2.8:
You who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, believe Him; 
And your reward shall not fail.
2.9:
You who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, have expectancy for good, 
And for everlasting joy and kindness.
2.10:
Look at the generations of old and see; 
Did any ever trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and were put to shame? 
Or did any remain in His reverence, and were forsaken? 
Or whom did He ever despise, that called upon Him?
2.11:
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is full of compassion and kindness, 
Patient, and very tender-hearted, and forgives sins, 
And saves in time of affliction.
2.12:
Woe unto fearful hearts, and faint hands, 
And the sinner that goes two ways!
2.14:
Woe unto you that have lost patience! 
And what shall you do when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall punish you?
2.15:
Those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall not disobey His Word; 
And those who love Him guard His Ways.
2.16:
Those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 seek that which is well-pleasing to Him; 
And those who love Him shall be filled with the Torah.
2.17:
Those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 prepare their hearts, 
And humble their beings in His sight,
2.18:
Saying, “We shall fall into the hands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and not into the hands of men; 
For as His excellence is, so is His kindness.”

20.1:
There is a reproof that is not proper; 
Again, some man holds his tongue, and he is wise.
20.2:
It is much better to reprove, than to be wroth secretly; 
And he who confesses his wrong shall be preserved from harm.
20.3:
How good is it, when you are reproved, to show repentance! 
For so you shall escape deliberate sin.
20.4:
As is the lust of a eunuch to defile a maiden; 
So is he who executes judgment with violence.
20.5:
There is one that keeps silent, and is found wise; 
And another by much babbling becomes hated.
20.6:
Some man holds his tongue, because he has no answer: 
And some keep silent, knowing his time.
20.7:
A wise man shall hold his tongue till he sees opportunity; 
But a babbler and a fool shall regard no time.
20.8:
He who uses many words shall be loathed; 
And he who takes authority for himself in this shall be hated.
20.9:
There is a sinner that has good success in evil; 
And there is a gain that turns to loss.
20.10:
There is a gift that shall not profit you; 
And there is a gift whose recompense is double.
20.11:
There is he who is shamed because of esteem; 
And there he who lifts up his head from a low estate.
20.12:
There is he who buys much for a little, 
But repays it sevenfold.
20.13:
A wise man by his words makes him beloved; 
But the favors of fools shall be poured out.
20.16:
The fool says, “I have no friends, 
I have no thanks for all my good deeds, 
And those who eat my bread speak evil of me.”
20.18:
To slip upon a pavement is better than to slip with the tongue; 
So shall the fall of the wicked come speedily.
20.19: An untimely word shall always be in the mouth of the unwise.
20.20:
A wise word shall be rejected when it comes from the mouth of a fool; 
For he shall not speak it in its season.
20.21:
There is he who is hindered from sinning through poverty; 
And when he takes rest, he is not troubled.
20.22:
There is he who destroys his own being through shame, 
And overthrows himself by showing partiality.
20.23:
There is he who promises to his friend from shame, 
And makes him his enemy for naught.
20.24:
A lie is an unclean stain within a man, 
Yet it is continually in the mouth of the unlearned.
20.25:
A thief is better than a man who is known to lie: 
But they shall both inherit destruction.
20.26:
The way of a liar is humiliation, 
And his shame is ever with him.
20.27:
With his words a wise man shall promote himself to esteem: 
And he who has understanding shall please great men.
20.28:
He who tills his land shall increase his heap: 
And he who pleases great men shall receive pardon for wrong.
20.29:
Presents and bribes blind the eyes of the wise, 
And stop up his mouth so he cannot reprove.
20.30:
Wisdom that is hidden, and treasure that is hoarded up, 
What profit is there in either?
20.31:
Better is he who hides his folly 
Than a man who hides his wisdom.
20.32:
Enduring patience in seeking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Is better than he who leads his life without a guide.

21.1:
My son, have you sinned? 
Do so no more, 
But ask forgiveness for your former sins.
21.2:
Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent; 
For if you come too close to it, it shall bite you. 
The teeth of it are as the teeth of a lion, 
Slaying the beings of men.
21.3:
All wickedness is as a two- edged sword, 
The wounds of which cannot be healed.
21.4:
Fear and wickedness shall waste wealth; 
Therefore the house of the proud shall be made desolate.
21.5:
A prayer out of a poor man's mouth reaches the ears of Elohim, 
And his right-ruling comes speedily.
21.6:
He who hates to be reproved is in the path of sinners; 
But he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall repent from his heart.
21.7:
A learned man is known far and near; 
And a man of understanding knows when he slips.
21.8:
He who builds his house with another man’s silver, 
Is like one that gathers stones for the tomb of his burial.
21.9:
The assembly of the wicked is like tow wrapped together; 
And their end is a flame of fire to destroy them.
21.10:
The way of sinners is paved with stones, 
But at the end of it is the pit of She’ol.
21.11:
He who guards the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gains understanding from it; 
And the perfect reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is wisdom.
21.12:
He who is not wise cannot be taught; 
But there is a knowledge which multiplies bitterness.
21.13:
The knowledge of a wise man shall increase as a flood: 
And his counsel is like a pure fountain of life.
21.14:
The inward parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, 
And he shall hold no knowledge as long as he lives.
21.15:
If a skilled man hears a wise word, 
He commends it, and adds to it; 
But when one of no understanding hears it, 
It displeases him, and he throws it behind his back.
21.16:
The talking of a fool is like a burden on the way; 
But favor shall be found in the lips of the wise.
21.17:
They inquire at the mouth of the wise in the assembly, 
And they shall consider his words in their heart.
21.18:
As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool; 
And the knowledge of the unwise are words without sense.
21.19:
Instruction to fools is as chains on the feet, 
And like shackles on the right hand.
21.20:
A fool lifts up his voice with laughter; 
But a wise man hardly smiles a little.
21.21:
Learning is to a wise man as an ornament of gold, 
And like a bracelet upon his right arm.
21.22:
The foot of a fool hurries into his house; 
But a diligent man is ashamed of him.
21.23:
A fool shall peep at the door into the house; 
But he who is disciplined shall stand outside.
21.24:
It is the disrespect of a man to listen at the door: 
But a wise man shall be grieved with the shame.
21.25:
The lips of gossipers speak that which does not pertain to them; 
But the words of those who have understanding are weighed in the balance.
21.26:
The heart of fools is in their mouth; 
But the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
21.27:
When the wicked curses an adversary, 
He curses his own being.
21.28: A whisperer defiles his own being, and is hated wherever he dwells.

22.1:
A lazy man is compared to a filthy stone, 
And all shall hiss him to shame.
22.2:
An idle man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: 
Every man that picks it up shall shake off his hand.
22.3:
An undisciplined man is the shame of his father that brought him forth; 
And a daughter is brought forth to his loss.
22.4:
A wise daughter brings an inheritance to her husband; 
But she who lives dishonestly is her father’s heaviness.
22.5:
She who is bold shames both her father and her husband, 
And they shall both despise her.
22.6:
An untimely word is music in mourning; 
But blows and discipline by wisdom are never untimely.
22.7:
Whoever teaches a fool is as one who glues a potsherd together, 
And as he who wakes one from a sound sleep.
22.8:
He who speaks a word to a fool speaks to one in a slumber; 
When he has spoken a word, he shall say, “What is this word?”
22.9:
If children live decently, and have means, 
They shall cover the lowliness of their parents.
22.10:
But children, being haughty, through pride and lacking discipline, 
Stain the nobility of their relatives.
22.11:
Weep for the dead, for he has lost the light; 
And weep for the fool, for he lacks understanding. 
Make little weeping for the dead, for he is at rest: 
But the life of the fool is worse than death.
22.12:
Seven days men shall mourn for the dead; 
But all the days of his life for a fool and a wicked man.
22.13:
Do not speak much with a fool, 
And do not go to he who has no understanding. 
Beware of him, lest you have trouble, 
And you shall never be defiled with his foolishness. 
Depart from him, and you shall find rest, 
And never be worried with madness.
22.14:
What is heavier than lead? 
And what is its name, but a fool?
22.15:
Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, 
Than a man without understanding.
22.16:
As timber girded and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking; 
So the heart that is established by wise counsel shall fear at no time.
22.17:
A heart rested upon a thought of understanding, 
Is as a lovely plastering on the wall of a gallery.
22.18:
Fences put on a high place shall never stand against the wind; 
So a fearful heart in the mind of a fool cannot stand against any fear.
22.19:
He who pricks the eye makes tears fall; 
And he who pricks the heart makes it show her knowledge.
22.20:
Whoever throws a stone at the birds frightens them away; 
And he who reproaches his friend breaks a friendship.
22.21:
Though you draw a sword against your friend, yet do not despair; 
For there may be a returning.
22.24:
As the clouds and smoke of a furnace goes before the fire; 
So reviling before blood.
22.25:
I shall not be ashamed to defend a friend; 
Nor shall I hide myself from him.
22.26:
But if any evil comes upon me because of him, 
Every one that hears it shall beware of him.
22.27:
Who shall appoint a guard before my mouth, 
And a seal of wisdom upon my lips, 
So I do not suddenly fall by them, 
And that my tongue does not destroy me?

23.1:
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Father and Aḏon of all my ḥai, 
Do not leave me to their counsels, 
And do not let me fall by them.
23.2:
Who shall appoint whips over my thoughts, 
And the discipline of wisdom over my heart? 
That they do not spare me for my ignorances, 
And it does not pass by my sins;
23.3:
Lest my ignorances increase, and my sins multiply to my destruction, 
And I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me, 
Whose expectancy is far from Your kindness.
23.4:
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Father and Elohim of my ḥai, 
Do not give me a proud look, 
But always turn your servants away from a haughty mind.
23.5:
Turn me away from worthless expectation and lust, 
And You hold up he who desires to always serve You.
23.6:
Do not let the gluttony of the stomach nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; 
And do not give me, your servant, over to a hardened heart.
23.7:
Hear O you children, the instruction of the mouth; 
He who guards it shall never be overtaken with his lips.
23.8:
The sinner shall be left in his foolishness; 
Both the speaker of evil and the proud shall fall by it.
23.9:
Do not accustom your mouth to swearing; 
Nor use the Name of the Qadosh One.
23.10:
For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a bruise; 
So he who swears Naming Elohim continually shall not be guiltless.
23.11:
A man that swears much is filled with wickedness, 
And the plague shall never depart from his house. 
If he transgresses, his sin shall be upon him; 
And if he does not acknowledge his sin, he commits a double offense: 
And if he swears in vain, he shall not be innocent, 
But his house shall be filled with calamities.
23.13:
Do not use your mouth to swear rashly, 
For in these words there is sin.
23.14:
Remember your father and your mother when you sit among great men. 
Do not be forgetful before them, and so, by your habit, 
Become a fool, and wish that you had not been born, 
And curse the day of your birth.
23.15:
The man who is accustomed to insulting words 
Shall never be instructed all the days of his life.
23.16:
Two kinds of men multiply sin, and the third shall bring wrath: 
A heated spirit as a burning fire shall never be quenched till it is consumed: 
One who whores in the body of his flesh shall never cease till he has kindled a fire.
23.17:
All bread is sweet to those who whore, 
He does not cease till he dies.
23.18:
An adulterer, says thus in his heart: 
“Who sees me? I am surrounded with darkness. 
“The walls cover me, and no one sees me; what do I need to fear? 
“The Most High shall not remember my sins.”
23.19:
Such a man only fears the eyes of men, 
And does not know that the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, 
Watching all the ways of men, and observing the most secret places.
23.20:
He knew all when they were created; 
So after they were accomplished he looked upon them all.
23.21:
This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, 
And he shall be taken where he does not suspect.
23.22:
So it shall also be for the wife that leaves her husband, 
And brings forth an heir by another.
23.24:
She shall be brought out into the assembly, 
And inquiry shall be made of her children.
23.25:
Her children shall not take root, 
And her branches shall not bring forth fruit.
23.26:
She shall leave a cursed remembrance, 
And her reproach shall not be blotted out.
23.27:
And those who remain shall know that there is none better than the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And that there is naught sweeter than to guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
23.28:
It is great esteem to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And to be accepted by Him is long life.

24.1:
Wisdom shall praise herself, 
And be esteemed in the midst of her people.
24.2:
In the assembly of the Most High she opens her mouth, 
And overcomes before His power.
24.3:
I came out of the mouth of the Most High, 
And covered the earth as a cloud.
24.4:
I dwelt in high places, 
And my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
24.5:
I alone surrounded the circuit of the shamayim, 
And walked in the bottom of the deep.
24.6:
In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, 
And in every people and nation, 
I obtained a possession.
24.7:
With all these I sought rest; 
And in whose inheritance shall I remain?
24.8:
So the Creator of all gave me a command, 
And He who made me gave rest for my tent, and said, 
“Let your dwelling be in Ya’aqoḇ, and your inheritance in Yisra’ĕl.”
24.9:
He created me from the beginning before the world, 
And I shall never fail.
24.10:
In the qodesh Mishkan I served before Him; 
And so I was established in Tsiyon.
24.11:
Likewise in the beloved city He gave me rest, 
And in Yerushalayim was my strength.
24.12:
And I took root in an esteemed people, 
Even in the portion of the inheritance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
24.13:
I was exalted like a cedar in Leḇanon, 
And as a cypress upon the mountains of Ḥermon.
24.14:
I was exalted like a palm tree in Ĕyn Geḏi, 
And as a rosebush in Yeriḥo, 
As a fair olive tree in a pleasant field, 
And grew as a fig tree by the water.
24.15:
I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon and rosewood, 
And I yielded a pleasant fragrance like the best myrrh, 
As galbanam, and shoham, and fragrant gum, 
And as the fragrance of frankincense in the Mishkan.
24.16:
As the cypress I stretched out my branches, 
And my branches are the branches of esteem and favor.
24.17:
As the vine I brought forth a pleasant fragrance, 
And my flowers are the fruit of esteem and wealth.
24.18:
I am the mother of pleasant love, and reverence, and knowledge, and qodesh expectancy: 
I therefore, being of old, 
Am given to all my children who are named by Him.
24.19:
Come to me, all you who desire me, 
And fill yourselves with my fruit.
24.20:
For my remembrance is sweeter than honey, 
And my inheritance than the honeycomb.
24.21:
Those who eat of me shall hunger for more, 
And those who drink me shall thirst for more.
24.22:
He who obeys me shall never be ashamed, 
And those who work beside me shall not do wrong.
24.23:
All these are the Book of the Covenant of the Most High Elohim, 
Even the Law which Mosheh Commanded for an inheritance to the congregations of Ya’aqoḇ.
24.25:
He fills all with His wisdom, 
As Pishon and as Ḥiddeqel in the time of first-fruits.
24.26:
He makes understanding to abound like Perath, 
And as the Yardĕn in the time of the harvest.
24.27:
He makes the instruction of knowledge appear as the light, 
And as Giḥon in the time of grape harvest.
24.28:
The first man did not know her fully; 
Nor shall the last find her out.
24.29:
For her thoughts are more than the sea, 
And her counsels deeper than the great deep.
24.30:
I also came out as a wadi from a river, 
And as a channel into a garden.
24.31:
I said, “I shall water my best garden, 
And shall water my garden bed very much.” 
And see, my wadi became a river, and my river became a sea.
24.32:
I shall yet make instruction to shine as the morning, 
And shall send forth her light far away.
24.33:
I shall yet pour out instruction as neḇuah, 
And leave it to all ages forever.
24.34:
See that I have not labored for myself only, 
But for all those who seek wisdom.

25.1:
In three matters I was adorned, 
And stood in loveliness both before Elohim and man: 
The oneness of brothers, the love of neighbors, 
A man and wife that agree together.
25.2:
Three sorts of men my being hates, 
And I greatly loathe of their life: 
A poor man who is proud, a wealthy man who is a liar, 
And an old adulterer who is foolish.
25.3:
If you have gathered naught in your youth, 
How shall you find any matter in your old age?
25.4:
O how lovely is judgment for grey hairs, 
And for the aged to know counsel!
25.5:
O how lovely is the wisdom of old men, 
And understanding and counsel in men of esteem.
25.6:
Much experience is the crown of old men, 
And the reverence of Elohim is their esteem.
25.7:
There are nine which I have judged in my heart to be happy, 
And the tenth I shall relate with my tongue: 
A man that has joy from his children; 
And he who lives to see the fall of his enemy.
25.8:
Ashrĕ is he who dwells with a wife of understanding, 
And that has not slipped with his tongue, 
And that has not served a man more unworthy than himself.
25.9:
Ashrĕ is he who has found insight, 
And he who speaks in the ears of those who listen.
25.10:
O how great is he who finds wisdom! 
Yet there is none above he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
25.11:
But the love of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 passes all in understanding; 
He who possesses it, to what shall he be likened?
25.12:
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the beginning of His love; 
And belief is the beginning of clinging to Him.
25.13:
Any wound, but a wound of the heart; 
And any wickedness, but the wickedness of a woman.
25.14:
And any affliction, but the affliction from those who hate me; 
And any revenge, but the revenge of enemies.
25.15:
There is no venom above the venom of a serpent; 
And there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy.
25.16:
I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, 
Than to dwell in a house with a wicked woman.
25.17:
The wickedness of a woman changes her appearance, 
And darkens her face like sackcloth.
25.18:
Her husband shall sit among his neighbors; 
And listening he shall sigh bitterly.
25.19:
All wickedness is but little to the wickedness of a woman; 
Let the portion of a sinner fall upon her.
25.20:
As the climbing of a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, 
So is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
25.21:
Do not stumble at the loveliness of a woman, 
And do not desire her for pleasure.
25.22:
A woman supporting her husband, 
Is full of wrath, hardness, and much reproach.
25.23:
A wicked woman causes courage to cease, 
Causes a heavy face and a wounded heart; 
A woman that does not comfort her husband in distress 
Causes weak hands and feeble knees.
25.24:
From the woman came the beginning of sin, 
And because of her we all die.
25.25:
Give water no outlet; 
Nor a wicked woman freedom to roam.
25.26:
If she does not do as you would have her, 
Cut her off from yourself, 
And give her a certificate of divorce, and let her go.

26.1:
Ashrĕ is the man that has a capable wife, 
For the number of his days shall be double.
26.2:
A capable woman gladdens her husband, 
And he shall fill the years of his life in peace.
26.3:
A good wife is a good portion, 
Which shall be given in the portion of those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.4:
Whether a man is wealthy or poor, 
If he has a good heart toward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
He shall rejoice at all times with a cheerful face.
26.6:
But a woman that is jealous over another woman is grieving to the heart and sorrow; 
And a lashing tongue which makes known to all.
26.7:
An evil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro; 
He who has hold of her is as though he held a scorpion.
26.8:
A drunken and wandering woman causes great wrath, 
And she does not cover her own shame.
26.9: The whoring of a woman is known by her haughty looks and eyelids.
26.10:
If your daughter is wayward, keep her straight, 
Lest she abuse herself through too much freedom.
26.11:
Watch over one with a hard eye; 
And do not marvel if she trespasses against you.
26.12:
She shall open her mouth, as a thirsty traveler who has found a fountain, 
And drink of every water near her. 
By every hedge she shall sit down, 
And open her quiver for every arrow.
26.13:
The favor of a wife delights her husband, 
And her discretion shall fatten his bones.
26.14:
A silent and loving woman is a gift of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; 
And there is naught worth as much as a mind well instructed.
26.15:
A humble and trustworthy woman is a double favor, 
And her sober mind cannot be valued.
26.16:
As the sun when it rises high in the shamayim; 
So is the loveliness of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
26.17:
As the shining light upon the qodesh candlestick; 
So is the loveliness of the face in ripe age.
26.18:
As the golden stands upon the sockets of silver; 
So are the lovely feet with a constant heart.
26.19:
My son, guard the flower of your youth well; 
And do not give your strength to foreigners.
26.20:
When you have acquired a fruitful possession through all the field, 
Sow it with your own seed, trusting in the goodness of your stock.
26.21:
So your relatives which you leave are made great, 
Having the confidence of their good genealogy.
26.22:
A whore shall be counted as spittle; 
But a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.
26.23:
A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man; 
But a reverent woman is given to he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.24:
A dishonest woman is despised and shamed; 
But an honest woman shall revere her husband.
26.25:
A headstrong woman shall be counted as a dog; 
But she that is humble reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
26.26:
A woman that esteems her husband shall be judged wise among all; 
But she that shames him in her pride shall be counted wicked among all.
26.27: A loud-mouthed woman and a nagger shall be sought out to drive away the enemies.
26.29:
A merchant hardly guards himself from doing wrong; 
And a trader is not free from sin.

27.1:
Many have sinned for a small matter; 
And he who seeks abundance turns his eyes away.
27.2:
As a nail holds fast between the join of stones; 
So sin holds close between buying and selling.
27.3:
Unless a man behaves diligently in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
His house shall soon be overthrown.
27.4:
As when one sifts with a sieve, the refuse remains; 
So the filth of man is in his words.
27.5:
The furnace tries the potter’s vessels; 
So the trial of man is in his reasoning.
27.6:
The fruit declares if the tree has been cultivated; 
So is the speaking of pride in the heart of man.
27.7:
Praise no man before you hear him speak; 
For this is the trial of men.
27.8:
If you follow righteousness, you shall obtain it, 
And put it on, as a long robe of esteem.
27.9:
The birds shall gather with their kind; 
So shall truth return to those who practice it.
27.10:
As the lion lies in wait for prey; 
So does sin for those who work wickedness.
27.11:
The words of a reverent man are always with wisdom; 
But a fool changes as the moon.
27.12:
Watch the time if you are among the foolish; 
But be continually among men of understanding.
27.13:
The words of fools are troublesome, 
And their entertainment is the indecency of sin.
27.14:
The words of he who swears much makes the hair stand upright; 
And their uproar makes one stop his ears.
27.15:
The strife of the proud is bloodshed, 
And their revilings are grievous to the ear.
27.16:
Whoever uncovers secrets loses his trust; 
And shall never find a friend of his being.
27.17:
Love your friend, and be trustworthy to him; 
But if you betray his secrets, never again follow after him.
27.18:
For as a man has destroyed his enemy; 
So you have lost the love of your neighbor.
27.19:
As one that releases a bird out of his hand, 
So you have let your neighbor go, 
And shall not have him again.
27.20:
Do not follow after him, for he is too far off; 
He is like a gazelle escaped out of the snare.
27.22:
He who winks with the eyes works evil; 
And he who knows him departs from him.
27.23:
When you are present, he shall speak sweetly, and shall admire your words; 
But in the end he shall twist his mouth, and slander your sayings.
27.24:
I have hated many matters, but naught like him; 
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall hate him.
27.25:
Whoever throws a stone high, throws it on his own head; 
And a blow in deceit makes wounds.
27.26:
Whoever digs a pit shall fall in to it; 
And he who lays a trap shall be caught in it.
27.27:
He who does evil, it shall fall upon him, 
And he shall not know from where it comes.
27.28:
Mockery and reproach are from the proud; 
But vengeance as a lion, lies in wait for them.
27.29:
Those who rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; 
And anguish shall consume them before they die.
27.30:
Evil and wrath, even these are abominations; 
And the sinful man has them both.

28.1:
He who is vengeful shall find vengeance from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And He shall surely keep account of his sins.
28.2:
Forgive your neighbor the harm that he has done to you, 
So your sins shall also be forgiven when you pray.
28.3:
One man bears hatred against another, 
And should he seek forgiveness from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
28.4:
He shows no kindness to a man, who is like himself; 
And does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?
28.5:
If he who is but flesh maintains hatred, 
Who shall pray forgiveness for his sins?
28.6:
Remember your end, and let enmity cease; 
Corruption and death, and remain in the Commands.
28.7:
Remember the Commands, and bear no evil against your neighbor; 
The Covenant of the Most High, and overlook faults.
28.8:
Abstain from strife, and you shall diminish your sins; 
For a man of rage kindles strife,
28.9:
A sinful man disrupts friendships, 
And creates quarrels among those who are at peace.
28.11:
A hasty quarrel kindles a fire; 
And hasty fighting sheds blood.
28.13:
Curse the gossiper and double tongued; 
For such have destroyed many who were at peace.
28.14:
A backbiting tongue has troubled many, and driven them from nation to nation: 
It has pulled down strong cities, and overthrown the houses of great men.
28.15:
A backbiting tongue has thrown out virtuous women, 
And deprived them of their labors.
28.16: Whoever listens to it shall never find rest, and never dwell quietly.
28.17:
The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh; 
But the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.
28.18:
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword; 
But not as many who have fallen by the tongue.
28.19:
Ashrĕ is he who is protected from its venom; 
Who has not drawn its yoke, nor been bound in its bands.
28.20:
For its yoke is a yoke of iron, 
And its bands are bands of bronze.
28.21:
The death from it is an evil death; 
The grave is better than it.
28.22:
It shall not rule over those who revere Elohim, 
Nor shall they be burned with its flame.
28.23:
Those who forsake 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall fall into it; 
And it shall burn in them, and not be quenched. 
It shall be sent upon them as a lion, 
And devour them as a leopard.
28.24:
As you hedge your possessions with thorns around, 
And bind up your silver and gold,
28.25:
Weigh your words in a balance, 
And make a door and bar for your mouth.
28.26:
Beware you do not slip by it, 
Lest you fall before he who lies in wait.

29.1:
He who is kind shall lend to his neighbor; 
And he who strengthens his hand guards the Commands.
29.2:
Lend to your neighbor in his time of need, 
And repay your neighbor again in due season.
29.3:
Guard your word, and deal trustworthily with him, 
And you shall always find that which is necessary for you.
29.4:
Many reckon what was loaned to them to be found, 
And put to trouble those who helped them.
29.6:
If he overcomes, he shall hardly give the half, 
And he shall count it as though he had found it. 
If not, he has deprived him of his silver, and he has gained an enemy without cause. 
He pays him with cursings and slander; 
And instead of esteem he shall pay him shame.
29.7:
Many have therefore refused to lend for other men’s evil deeds, 
Fearing to be cheated.
29.8:
Yet have patience with a man in poverty, 
And do not delay to show him kindness.
29.9:
Help the poor for the sake of the Command, 
And do not turn him away because of his poverty.
29.10:
Lose your silver for your brother and your friend, 
And do not let it rust under a stone to be lost.
29.11:
Lay up your treasure according to the Commands of the Most High, 
And it shall bring you more profit than gold.
29.12:
Store up kind deeds in your storehouses, 
And it shall deliver you from all affliction.
29.13: It shall fight for you against your enemies better than a mighty shield and strong spear.
29.14:
An honest man stands guarantor for his neighbor; 
But he who is impudent shall forsake him.
29.15:
Do not forgot the friendship of your guarantor, 
For he has given his life for you.
29.16: A sinner shall overthrow the good manner of his guarantor;
29.17: And he who is thankless shall forsake he who delivered him.
29.18:
Guarantee has undone many of good estate, 
And shaken them as a wave of the sea. 
It has driven mighty men from their houses, 
So that they wandered among foreign nations.
29.19:
A wicked man transgressing the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall fall in guarantee; 
And he who undertakes and follows other men’s business for gain shall fall into lawsuits.
29.20:
Assist your neighbor according to your ability, 
And beware that you do not fall into the same.
29.21:
The necessities for life are water, and bread, and garments, 
And a house for privacy.
29.22:
Better is the life of a poor man in a lowly cottage, 
Than food of delicacies in another man’s house.
29.23:
Whether little or much, be content, 
That you do not hear the reproach of your house.
29.24:
For it is a miserable life to go from house to house; 
For where you are a stranger, you dare not open your mouth.
29.25:
You shall entertain, and feast, and have no thanks; 
And you shall hear bitter words:
29.26:
“Come, you stranger, and furnish a table, 
And feed me of what you have ready.
29.27:
“Give place, you stranger, to an esteemed man; 
My brother seeks lodging, and I have need of my house.”
29.28:
These matters are grievous to a man of understanding; 
The contempt of a household, and a reproach of the lender.

3.1: Hear me your father, O children, and do accordingly, that you may be safe.
3.2:
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given the father esteem over the children, 
And has confirmed the authority of the mother over the sons.
3.3: Whoever esteems his father makes an atonement for his sins;
3.4: And he who esteems his mother is as one who stores up treasure.
3.5:
Whoever esteems his father shall have joy from his own children; 
And when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.
3.6:
He who esteems his father shall have a long life; 
And he who is obedient to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be a comfort to his mother.
3.7:
He who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall esteem his father, 
And shall do service unto his parents, as to his masters.
3.8:
Esteem your father and mother both in word and deed, 
That a beraḵah may come upon you from them.
3.9:
For the beraḵah of the father establishes the houses of children; 
But the curse of the mother roots out foundations.
3.10:
Do not rejoice in the shame of your father; 
For your father’s shame is no esteem unto you.
3.11:
For the esteem of a man is from the esteem of his father; 
And a mother in shame is a reproach to the children.
3.12:
My son, help your father in his age, 
And do not grieve him as long as he lives.
3.13:
And if his understanding fails, have patience with him; 
And do not despise him when you are in your full strength.
3.14:
For the relief for your father shall not be forgotten; 
And instead of sin, it shall be added to build you up.
3.15:
In the day of your affliction it shall be remembered; 
Your sins also shall melt away, as the ice in the fair warm weather.
3.16:
He who forsakes his father is as a blasphemer; 
And he who displeases his mother is cursed of Elohim.
3.17:
My son, go on with your business in meekness; 
So you shall be beloved of He who approves.
3.18:
The greater you are, the more you humble yourself, 
And you shall find favor before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.19:
Many are in high places, and of name; 
But mysteries are revealed to the meek.
3.20:
For the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is great, 
And He is esteemed by the lowly.
3.21:
Do not search out that which is too hard for you, 
Neither seek that which is above your strength.
3.22:
But what is Commanded, think upon this with reverence, 
For it is not necessary for you to see with your eyes that which is secret.
3.23:
Do not be curious in unnecessary matters: 
For more is revealed to you than men understand.
3.24:
For many are deceived by their own worthless opinion; 
And evil suspicion has overthrown their judgment.
3.25:
Without eyes there is no light; 
Do not profess the knowledge which you do not have.
3.26:
A stubborn heart shall suffer evil in the end; 
And he who loves danger shall perish in it.
3.27:
A hard heart shall be loaded with sorrows; 
And the wicked man shall heap sin upon sin.
3.28:
In the punishment of the proud there is no remedy; 
For the plant of wickedness has taken root in him.
3.29:
The heart of the clever shall understand a parable; 
And an attentive ear is the desire of a wise man.
3.30:
Water shall quench a flaming fire; 
And kind deeds make an atonement for sins.
3.31:
And he who repays good deeds remembers that which may come after; 
And when he falls, he shall find a support.

30.1:
He who loves his son causes him to often feel the rod, 
That he may have joy from him in the end.
30.2:
He who punishes his son shall have joy in him, 
And shall rejoice in him among his acquaintances.
30.3:
He who teaches his son grieves the enemy; 
And before his friends he shall rejoice in him.
30.4:
Though his father dies, it is as though he were not dead; 
For he has left one behind who is like himself.
30.5:
While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: 
And when he died, he was not grieved.
30.6:
He left behind an avenger against his enemies, 
And one that shall repay kindness to his friends.
30.7:
He who makes too much of his son binds up his wounds; 
And his body shall be troubled at every cry.
30.8:
A horse unbroken becomes headstrong: 
And a child left to himself shall be unruly.
30.9:
Spoil your child, and he shall cause you dread; 
Play with him, and he shall bring you to grief.
30.10:
Do not laugh with him, lest you have sorrow from him, 
And lest you gnash your teeth in the end.
30.11:
Give him no freedom in his youth, 
And do not wink at his foolishness.
30.12:
Bow down his neck while he is young, 
And beat his side while he is a child, 
Lest he become stubborn, and be disobedient to you, 
And so bring sorrow to your heart.
30.13:
Discipline your son, and put him to work, 
Lest his wicked behavior be a stumbling to you.
30.14:
Better is the poor, being healthy and strong in body, 
Than a wealthy man who is afflicted in his body.
30.15:
Health and good state of body are better than any gold, 
And a strong body above infinite wealth.
30.16:
There is no wealth above a healthy body, 
And no joy above the joy of the heart.
30.17: Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness.
30.18:
Delicacies poured upon a closed mouth, 
Are as servings of meat placed upon a grave.
30.20:
He sees with his eyes and groans, 
As a eunuch that embraces a maiden and sighs.
30.21:
Do not give your mind over to sorrow, 
And do not afflict yourself on purpose.
30.22:
The gladness of the heart is the life of man, 
And the joy of a man prolongs his days.
30.24:
Envy and wrath shorten the life, 
And worry brings age before time.
30.25: A cheerful and good heart pays attention to his meat and diet.

31.1:
Watching for wealth consumes the flesh, 
And the worry of it drives away sleep.
31.2:
Watchful worry does not let a man slumber, 
As a painful disease breaks sleep.
31.3:
The wealthy labors greatly in gathering wealth together; 
And when he rests, he is filled with his delicacies.
31.4:
The poor labors in his poverty; 
And when he finishes, he is still needy.
31.5:
He who loves gold shall not be declared right, 
And he who pursues corruption shall have enough.
31.6:
Gold has been the ruin of many, 
And their destruction stands.
31.7:
It is a stumbling block to those who offer to it, 
And every fool shall be taken in it.
31.8:
Ashrĕ is the wealthy who is found without blemish, 
And has not gone after gold.
31.9:
Who is he, that we may call him happy? 
For he has done wonders among his people.
31.10:
Who has been tried by it, and found perfect? 
Then let him boast. 
Who might offend, and has not offended? 
Or may do evil, and has not done it?
31.11:
His goods shall be established, 
And the assembly shall declare his kind deeds.
31.12:
If you sit at a plentiful table, do not be greedy on it, 
And do not say, “There is much food on it.”
31.14:
Do not stretch your hand wherever you look, 
And do not thrust with it into the dish.
31.15:
Do not judge your neighbor by yourself; 
But be discerning in every matter.
31.16:
Eat as is allowed, that which is put before you; 
But do not devour, lest you be hated.
31.17:
For the sake of manners, be first to cease; 
And do not be gluttonous, lest you cause stumbling.
31.18:
When you sit among many, 
Do not be the first to reach out your hand.
31.19:
A very little is sufficient for a man of discipline, 
And he is not short of breath on his bed.
31.21:
And if you have been forced to eat, 
Rise up, go vomit, and you shall have rest.
31.22:
My son, listen to me, and do not despise me, 
And in the end you shall find as I told you. 
In all your work be efficient, so that no sickness comes to you.
31.23:
Whoever is generous with his food, men shall speak well of him; 
And the report of his good hospitality shall be believed.
31.24:
But against he who is greedy with his food, the whole city shall murmur; 
And the report of his selfishness shall not be doubted.
31.25:
Do not show your boldness with wine; 
For wine has destroyed many.
31.26:
The furnace proves the sword edge by dipping; 
So wine tries the hearts of the proud in drunkenness.
31.27:
Wine is as good as life to a man, if it is drunk moderately. 
What then is life to a man that is without wine? 
For it was made to make men glad.
31.28:
Wine drunk moderately and in season brings gladness of the heart, 
And cheerfulness of the mind;
31.29:
But wine drunken in excess makes bitterness of the mind, 
With brawling and quarreling.
31.30:
Drunkenness increases the rage of a fool till he stumbles: 
It diminishes strength, and causes wounds.

32.1:
If you are appointed master do not lift yourself up, 
But be among them as one of the rest. 
Diligently look after them, and then sit down.
32.2:
And when you have fulfilled your office, take your place, 
That you may rejoice with them, 
And receive a crown for your well ordering of the feast.
32.3:
Speak, you who are the elder, for it is fitting for you, 
But with right-ruling; and do not withhold music.
32.4:
Do not pour out words when there is a musician, 
And do not put forth wisdom out of time.
32.5: A concert of music at a banquet of wine is as a signet of ruby mounted in gold.
32.6:
As a signet of an emerald mounted in a work of gold, 
So is the melody of music with pleasant wine.
32.7:
Speak, young man, if there is need of you; 
And yet only twice when you are asked.
32.8:
Let your words be few, saying much with few words; 
Be as one who knows and yet holds his tongue.
32.9:
If you are among great men, do not make yourself equal with them; 
And when aged men are in place, do not use many words.
32.10:
Before the thunder goes lightning; 
And before a humble man goes favor.
32.11:
Rise up early, and do not be the last; 
And get home without delay.
32.12:
There fulfill your office, and do what you shall: 
But do not sin with proud speech.
32.13:
And for these baraḵ Him who made you, 
And has filled you with His goodness.
32.14:
Whoever reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall receive His discipline; 
And those who seek Him early shall find favor.
32.15:
He who seeks the Law shall be filled with it; 
But the hypocrite shall stumble over it.
32.16:
Those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall find Right-Ruling, 
And shall kindle righteousness as a light.
32.17:
A sinful man shall not be reproved, 
But finds an excuse according to his liking.
32.19:
Do no deed without advice; 
And when you are done, do not regret it.
32.20:
Do not go in a way in which you may fall, 
And do not stumble among the stones.
32.21: Do not be reckless on an easy road.
32.22: And beware of your own children.
32.23:
In every good work guard your own being; 
For this is the keeping of the Commands.
32.24:
He who believes in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 guards the Commands; 
And he who trusts in Him does not come to harm.

33.1:
No evil shall come upon he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; 
And in trials He also shall deliver him.
33.2:
A wise man does not hate the Law; 
But he who is a hypocrite in it, is like a ship in a storm.
33.3:
A man of understanding trusts in the Law; 
And the Law is trustworthy to him, as a Word.
33.4:
Prepare what to say, and so you shall be heard; 
And draw upon instruction, and then give answer.
33.5:
The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; 
And his thoughts are like a rolling axle.
33.6:
A mocking friend is like a stallion, 
He neighs under everyone that rides him.
33.7:
Why is one day better than another, 
When all the light of every day of the year is from the sun?
33.8:
By the knowledge of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 they were appointed; 
And He turns seasons and Feasts.
33.9:
Some of them He has made High Days, and qadosh them, 
And some of them He has made regular days.
33.10:
And all men are from the ground, 
And Aḏam was created from the earth.
33.11:
In much knowledge 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spread them, 
And made their ways different.
33.12:
Some of them He has baraḵ and exalted, 
And some of them He qadosh, and placed near Himself; 
But some of them He has cursed and brought low, 
And removed from their places.
33.14:
Good opposes evil, and life against death; 
So is the righteous against the sinner, and the wicked against the reverent.
33.15:
So look upon all the works of the Most High; 
And there are pairs of two, one against another.
33.16:
I woke up last of all, as one that gathers after the grape gatherers; 
By the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 I profited, and trod my winepress like a gatherer of grapes.
33.17:
Consider that I did not labor for myself only, 
But for all those who seek learning.
33.18:
Hear me, O you great men of the people, 
And listen with your ears, you rulers of the assembly.
33.20:
As long as you live and have breath in you, 
Do not give yourself over to any.
33.21:
For it is better that your children should seek from you, 
Than that you should stand to their sympathy.
33.22:
Be the best in all your works; 
Do not leave a blot on your esteem.
33.23:
At the time when you shall end your days, and finish your life, 
Distribute your inheritance.
33.24:
Fodder, a rod, and burdens, are for the donkey; 
And bread, discipline, and work, for a servant.
33.25:
If you put your servant to labor, you shall find rest: 
But if you let him go idle, he shall seek freedom.
33.26:
A yoke and a collar bow the neck; 
So are tortures and punishment for an evil servant.
33.27:
Send him to work, so he is not idle; 
For idleness teaches much evil.
33.28:
Put him to work, as is fit for him; 
If he is not obedient, put on heavier shackles.
33.29:
But do not be excessive toward any; 
And do naught without discretion.
33.30:
If you have a servant, let him be to you as yourself, 
Because you have bought him for a price.
33.31:
If you have a servant, treat him as a brother; 
For you have need of him, as of your own being. 
If you treat him evilly, and he runs from you, 
Which way shall you go to seek him?

34.1:
The expectancies of a man of no understanding are empty and false; 
And dreams raise up fools.
34.2:
Whoever regards dreams is like he who catches at a shadow, 
And follows after the wind.
34.3:
The vision of dreams is the reflection of one to another, 
Even as the likeness of a face to a face.
34.4:
From an unclean matter, what may be cleansed? 
And from that which is false, what truth shall come?
34.6:
If they are not sent from the Most High in your visitation, 
Do not lay your heart upon them.
34.7:
For dreams have deceived many, 
And they have failed those who put their trust in them.
34.8:
The Law shall be found perfect without falsehood; 
And wisdom is perfection to a trustworthy mouth.
34.9:
A man that has travelled knows much; 
And he who has much experience shall declare wisdom.
34.10:
He who has no experience knows little; 
But he who has travelled is full of insight.
34.11:
When I travelled, I saw much; 
And I understand more than I could express.
34.12:
I was often in danger of death; 
Yet I was delivered because of these:
34.13:
The spirit of those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall live; 
For their expectancy is in He who saves them.
34.14:
Whoever reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall not fear nor be afraid; 
For He is his expectancy.
34.15:
Ashrĕ is the being of he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: 
To whom does he look, and who is his strength?
34.16:
For the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are upon those who love Him, 
He is their mighty shield and strong support, 
A protection from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon, 
A preservation from stumbling, and a help from falling.
34.17:
He raises up the being, and lightens the eyes: 
He gives health, ḥai, and beraḵah.
34.18:
He who offers of what is wrongfully gotten, his offering is a mockery; 
And the gifts of unrighteous men are not accepted.
34.19:
The Most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; 
Nor is He appeased by the multitude of offerings for sin.
34.20:
Whoever brings an offering from the goods of the poor, 
Does as one that kills the son before his father’s eyes.
34.21:
The bread of the needy is their life; 
He who deprives him of it is a man of blood.
34.22:
He who takes away the livelihood of his neighbor slays him; 
And he who deprives the laborer of his wage is a shedder of blood.
34.23:
When one builds, and another pulls down, 
What profit do they have but labor?
34.24:
When one prays, and another curses, 
Whose voice shall 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hear?
34.25:
He who washes himself after touching a dead body, 
If he touches it again, what use is his washing?
34.26:
So it is with a man that fasts for his sins, and goes again, and does the same; 
Who shall hear his prayer, or what does his humbling profit him?

35.1:
He who guards the Law brings offerings enough; 
He who guards the Command offers a peace offering.
35.2:
He who repays a good deed offers fine flour; 
And he who gives in kindness offers praise.
35.3:
To depart from wickedness is pleasing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; 
And to forsake unrighteousness is an atonement.
35.4: You shall not appear empty- handed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
35.5: For all these are because of the Command.
35.6:
The offering of the righteous makes the altar fat, 
And its sweet savor is before the Most High.
35.7:
The offering of a righteous man is acceptable. 
And the remembrance of it shall never be forgotten.
35.8:
Give 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 His esteem with a good eye, 
And do not diminish the first-fruits of your hands.
35.9:
In all your gifts show a cheerful face, 
And dedicate your tithes with gladness.
35.10:
Give to the Most High according to His enrichment unto you; 
And as you have received, give with a cheerful eye.
35.11:
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 repays, 
And shall give you seven times as much.
35.13:
He shows no partiality against the poor, 
But shall hear the prayer of the oppressed.
35.14:
He shall not despise the prayer of the fatherless; 
Nor the widow, when she pours out her complaint.
35.15:
Do not the tears run down the widow’s cheeks? 
And is not her cry against he who causes them to fall?
35.16:
He who 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 serves shall be accepted with favor, 
And his prayer reaches to the clouds.
35.19:
Till He has given to everyone according to their deeds, 
And to the works of men according to their schemes; 
Till He has judged the cause of His people, 
And caused them to rejoice in His kindness.
35.20:
Favor is welcomed in the time of affliction, 
As clouds of rain in the time of drought.

36.1: Show favor upon us, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of all, and look on us;
36.2: And send Your fear upon all the nations that do not seek You.
36.3:
