Lift up Your hand against the foreign nations, 
And let them see Your strength.
36.4:
As You were qadosh in us before them: 
So You be exalted among them before us.
36.5:
And let them know You, as we have known You, 
That there is no Elohim but You alone, O Elohim.
36.7:
Raise up displeasure, and pour out wrath; 
Remove the adversary, and destroy the enemy.
36.8:
Shorten the time, remember the Covenant, 
And let them declare Your wonders.
36.9:
Let he who escapes be consumed by the rage of the fire; 
And let those who oppress the people perish.
36.10:
Crush the heads of the rulers of the gentiles that say, 
“There is no one else but us!”
36.11:
Gather all the tribes of Ya’aqoḇ together; 
Your inheritance, as from the beginning.
36.12:
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, show favor upon the people that are called by Your Name, 
And upon Yisra’ĕl, whom You have named Your first-born.
36.13:
O be kind to Yerushalayim, Your qodesh city, 
The place of Your rest.
36.14:
Fill Tsiyon with Your unspeakable words, 
And Your people with Your esteem.
36.15:
Give witness to those who You have possessed from the beginning, 
And raise up neḇi’im that are for Your Name.
36.16:
Reward those who wait for You, 
And let Your neḇi’im be found trustworthy.
36.17:
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, hear the prayer of Your servants, 
According to the beraḵah of Aharon over Your people, 
That all those who dwell on the earth may know that You are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
The Elohim of old.
36.18:
The stomach consumes all foods, 
Yet one meat is better than another.
36.19:
As the mouth tastes different kinds of game; 
So does a heart of understanding false speeches.
36.20:
A crooked heart causes grief; 
But a man of experience shall repay him.
36.21:
A woman shall accept any man, 
Yet one daughter is better than another.
36.22:
The loveliness of a woman cheers the face, 
And there is naught a man loves better.
36.23:
If there is kindness, meekness, and comfort, in her tongue, 
Then her husband is not like other men.
36.24:
He who acquires a wife begins a possession, 
A help like himself, and a pillar of rest.
36.25:
Where no wall is, there possessions are plundered; 
And he who has no wife shall wander about sighing.
36.26:
Who shall trust a crafty thief that skips from city to city? 
Even so a man that has no house, and lodges wherever the night takes him?

37.1:
Every friend says, “I am his friend also.” 
But there is a friend, which is only a friend in name.
37.2:
Is it not a grief unto death, 
When a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?
37.3:
O wicked thoughts, where have you come from, 
To cover the earth with deceit?
37.4:
There is a companion, who rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, 
But in the time of trouble shall be against him.
37.5:
There is a companion, who helps his friend for his stomach, 
And takes up a shield against the enemy.
37.6:
Do not forget your friend in your heart, 
And do not forget him in your wealth.
37.7:
Every counsellor extolls counsel; 
But some who counsel for themselves.
37.9:
And say to you, “Your way is good.” 
And afterward stand on the other side, to see what shall befall you.
37.10:
Do not consult with one that suspects you; 
And hide your counsel from those who envy you.
37.12:
But be continually with a reverent man, 
Whom you know to guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Whose, mind is according to your mind, 
And shall grieve with you, if you fail.
37.13:
And let the counsel of your own heart stand; 
For there is no man more trustworthy to you than it.
37.14:
For the mind of a man sometimes tells him more than seven watchmen, 
That sit above in a high tower.
37.15:
And above all this, pray to the Most High, 
That He directs your way in truth.
37.16:
Let reason go before every work, 
And counsel before every action.
37.17: The face is a sign of changing of the heart.
37.19:
There is one who is wise and teaches many, 
And yet does not profit himself.
37.20:
There is one who shows wisdom in words, and is hated; 
He shall be destitute of all food.
37.21:
For favor is not given to him from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Because he has neglected all wisdom.
37.22:
Another is wise to himself; 
And the fruits of understanding are as praise in his mouth.
37.23:
A wise man instructs his people; 
And the fruits of his understanding do not fail.
37.24:
A wise man shall be filled with bireḵoth; 
And all those who see him shall regard him as happy.
37.25:
The days of the life of man may be numbered; 
But the days of Yisra’ĕl are without number.
37.26:
A wise man shall inherit esteem among his people, 
And his name shall be forever.
37.27:
My son, prove your being in your life, 
And see what is evil for it, and do not give in to it.
37.28:
For not all is profitable for all men, 
Nor has every being pleasure in every matter.
37.29:
Do not be gluttonous in any delicacy, 
Nor too greedy with food;
37.30:
For excess of food brings sickness, 
And gluttony shall turn to disgust.
37.31:
Many have perished by gluttony; 
But he who guards himself prolongs his life.

38.1:
Esteem a physician with the esteem due to him for the uses which you may have for him: 
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has created him.
38.2:
For healing comes from the Most High, 
And He shall receive esteem from the meleḵ.
38.3:
The skill of the physician shall raise his head; 
And in the sight of great men he shall be admired.
38.4:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has created medicines out of the earth; 
And he who is wise does not reject them.
38.5:
Was not the water made sweet with wood, 
That its power might be known?
38.6:
And He has given men skill, 
That He might be esteemed by His marvelous works.
38.7: With such He heals and takes away their pains.
38.9:
My son, in your sickness do not be slack; 
But pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He shall heal you.
38.10:
Cease from sin, and order your hands well, 
And cleanse your heart from all wickedness.
38.11:
Offer a sweet fragrance, and a remembrance of fine flour; 
And make an offering of fat of your being.
38.12:
So give place to the physician, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has created him; 
Do not let him leave you, for you have need of him.
38.13: There is a time when there is good success in their hands.
38.14:
For they shall also pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
That He would prosper that which they give, 
For ease and health to prolong life.
38.15:
He who sins before his Maker, 
Let him fall in the hand of the physician.
38.16:
My son, let tears fall down over the dead, 
And begin to lament, as if you had suffered great harm yourself; 
And then cover his body according to the custom, 
And do not neglect his burial.
38.18: For from grief comes death, and heaviness of the heart destroys strength.
38.19:
In affliction sorrow also remains; 
And the life of the poor is the curse of the heart.
38.20:
Take no grief to heart; 
Drive it away, and remember the latter end.
38.21:
Do not forget it, for there is no returning again; 
You shall do him no good, but harm yourself.
38.22:
“Remember my judgment; for so shall yours be also... 
Yesterday for me, and today for you.”
38.23:
When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; 
And be comforted for him, when his spirit has departed from him.
38.24:
The wisdom of a learned man comes by opportunity of leisure; 
And he who has little business may become wise.
38.25:
How shall he who holds the plough attain wisdom, 
And who sharpens the goad, who drives oxen, and is occupied in their labor, and whose talk is of bulls?
38.26:
He gives his mind to making furrows; 
And is diligent to give the cattle fodder.
38.31:
All these rely on their hands, 
And everyone is skilled in his work.
38.32:
Without these a city cannot be inhabited; 
And they could not dwell where they do, nor go up and down.
38.34:
But they maintain the face of the world, 
And their desire is in the work of their craft.

39.1:
But he who gives his mind to the Law of the Most High, 
And is occupied in the study of it, 
Seeks out of all the ancient wisdom, and is occupied in neḇuoth.
39.2:
He guards the sayings of the men of name; 
And where wise parables are, he shall be there also.
39.3:
He shall seek out the secrets of proverbs, 
And speak of hidden parables.
39.5:
He applies his heart early to look to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who made him, 
And shall pray before the Most High, 
And opens his mouth in prayer, 
And makes supplication for his sins.
39.6:
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty acts, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding; 
He shall pour out wise sayings, and give thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his prayer.
39.7:
He shall guide his counsel and knowledge, 
And on His secrets he meditates.
39.8:
He reveals that which he has learned, 
And shall boast in the Law of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
39.10:
Nations shall speak of his wisdom, 
And the assembly shall declare his praise.
39.11:
If he dies, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: 
And if he lives, he shall increase it.
39.12:
Yet I have more to say, which I have thought upon; 
For I am filled as at the full moon.
39.13:
Listen to me, you qodesh children, 
And bud as a rose of the field growing by the wadi;
39.14:
And give a sweet fragrance as frankincense, and flourish as a lily. 
Send out a fragrance, and sing a song of praise, 
Baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in all His works.
39.15:
Exalt His Name, and extol His praise with the songs of your lips, and with harps, 
And in praising Him you shall say after this manner:
39.16:
All the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are exceedingly good, 
And whatever He commands shall be accomplished in due season.
39.17:
And none shall say, “What is this? 
Why is that?” 
For at an appropriate time they shall all be sought out: 
At His command the waters stood as a heap, 
And the reservoir of waters at the words of His mouth.
39.18:
Whatever pleases Him is done at His command; 
And none reverses His deliverance.
39.19:
The works of all flesh are before Him, 
And there is none hidden from His eyes.
39.20:
He sees from everlasting to everlasting; 
And there is no matter too marvelous for Him.
39.21:
A man need not say, “What is this? Why is that?” 
For He has made all for their uses.
39.22:
His beraḵah covered the dry land as a river, 
And watered it as a flood.
39.23:
As He has turned the waters salty; 
So shall the gentiles inherit His wrath.
39.24:
As His ways are clear to the qodesh; 
So they are stumbling blocks to the wicked.
39.25:
The good matters are created for the good from the beginning; 
So evil matters for sinners.
39.26:
The basic necessities for the whole use of man’s life are: 
Water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the juice of grapes, and oil, and garments.
39.27:
All these are for good to the righteous; 
So to the sinners they are turned to evil.
39.28:
There are spirits that are created for punishment, 
Who in their wrath lay on many strokes; 
In the time of destruction they pour out their strength, 
And appease the wrath of He who made them.
39.29:
Fire, and hail, and scarcity of food, and death, 
All these were created for punishment;
39.30:
Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, 
And the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.
39.31:
They shall rejoice in His Command, and they shall be ready upon earth when needed; 
And when their time comes, they do not transgress His Word.
39.32:
Therefore from the beginning I knew, 
And thought upon these, and have left them in writing.
39.33:
All the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are good; 
And He shall give all that is needed in due season;
39.34:
So that a man cannot say, “This is worse than that.” 
For in time they all shall be prove good;
39.35:
And therefore praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all your heart and voice, 
And baraḵ the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

4.1:
My son, do not rob the poor of his living, 
And do not allow the needy eyes to wait long.
4.2:
Do not make a hungry being sorrowful; 
Neither provoke a man in his distress.
4.3:
Do not add more trouble to a heart that is tortured; 
And do not delay to give to he who is in need.
4.4:
Do not reject the supplication of the afflicted; 
Neither turn away your face from a poor man.
4.5:
Do not turn away your eye from the needy, 
And give him no occasion to curse you;
4.6:
For if he curses you in the bitterness of his being, 
His prayer shall be heard by He who made him.
4.7:
Earn for yourself the love of the assembly, 
And bow your head to a great man.
4.8:
Let it not grieve you to bend your ear to the poor, 
And give him a friendly answer with meekness.
4.9:
Deliver he who suffers wrong from the hand of the oppressor; 
And do not be faint-hearted when you sit in judgment.
4.10:
Be as a father to the fatherless, 
And like a husband to their mother; 
So you shall be as the Bĕn of the Most High, 
And He shall love you more than your mother does.
4.11:
Wisdom exalts her children, 
And lays hold of those who seek her.
4.12:
He who loves her loves ḥai; 
And those who seek her early shall be filled with joy.
4.13:
He who holds her fast shall inherit esteem; 
And wherever she enters, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall baraḵ.
4.14:
Those who serve her serve the Qadosh One: 
And those who love her 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 loves.
4.15:
Whoever gives ear to her shall judge the nations: 
And he who attends to her shall dwell securely.
4.16:
If a man commits himself to her, he shall inherit her; 
And his generation shall hold her in possession.
4.17:
For at first she shall walk by him in crooked ways, 
And bring fear and dread upon him, 
And punish him with her discipline, 
Until she may trust his being, and try him by her laws.
4.18:
Then she shall return him to the straight way, 
And comfort him, and show him her secrets.
4.19:
But if he goes wrong, she shall forsake him, 
And give him over to his own ruin.
4.20:
Watch for opportunity, and beware of evil; 
And do not be ashamed when it concerns your being.
4.21:
For there is shame that brings sin; 
And there is shame which is esteem and favor.
4.22:
Do not show partiality against your being, 
And do not let the fear of any man cause you to fall.
4.23:
And do not refrain to speak, when there is occasion to do good, 
And do not hide your wisdom in her loveliness.
4.24:
For by speech wisdom shall be known; 
And learning by the word of the tongue.
4.25:
By no means speak against the truth; 
But be ashamed of the straying of your ignorance.
4.26:
Do not be ashamed to confess your sins; 
And do not force the course of the river.
4.27:
Do not make yourself a servant to a foolish man; 
Neither show partiality to the mighty.
4.28:
Strive for the truth unto death, 
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall fight for you.
4.29:
Do not be hasty with your tongue, 
Or slack and negligent in your deeds.
4.30:
Do not be as a lion in your house, 
Nor wroth among your servants.
4.31:
Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive, 
And closed when you should repay.

40.1:
Great hardship is created for every man, 
And a heavy yoke is upon the sons of Aḏam; 
From the day that they go out of their mother’s womb, 
Till the day that they return to the mother of all.
40.2:
Their imagination of what is to come, and the day of death, 
Are their thoughts, and fear of heart;
40.3:
From he who sits on a throne of esteem, 
To he who is humbled in dirt and ashes;
40.4:
From he who wears purple and a crown, 
To he who is clothed with a linen robe.
40.5:
Wrath, and envy, trouble, and unrest, fear of death, and displeasure, and strife, 
And in the time of rest on his bed his sleep at night changes his knowledge.
40.6:
He gets little or no rest, and after his sleep, is as in a day of watching, 
Troubled in the vision of his mind, as if he had escaped out of a battle.
40.7:
When all is safe, he wakes, 
And marvels that the fear was naught.
40.8:
These come to all flesh, both man and beast, 
And seven times more upon sinners.
40.9:
Death, and bloodshed, strife, and sword, 
Calamities, scarcity of food, distress, and the scourge;
40.10:
These are created for the wicked, 
And the flood came for their sakes.
40.11:
All that are of the earth shall return to the earth again; 
And that which is of the waters returns to the sea.
40.12:
All bribery and unrighteousness shall be blotted out; 
But right-dealing endures forever.
40.13:
The goods of the unrighteous shall be dried up like a wadi, 
And shall vanish with noise, like great thunder in rain.
40.14:
While the generous shall rejoice; 
So transgressors shall come to naught.
40.15:
The children of the wicked shall not bring forth many branches; 
But are as unclean roots on a hard rock.
40.16:
The weed growing on all water and riverbank, 
Shall be pulled up before any grass.
40.17:
Kindness is like a garden of bireḵoth, 
And favor endures forever.
40.18:
To labor, and to be content with what a man has, is a sweet life; 
But he who finds a treasure is above them both.
40.19:
Children and the building of a city continue a man’s name; 
But a blameless wife is counted above them both.
40.20:
Wine and music rejoice the heart; 
But the love of wisdom is above them both.
40.21:
The flute and the harp make a sweet melody; 
But a pleasant tongue is above them both.
40.22:
Your eye desires favor and loveliness; 
But more than both is grain while green.
40.23:
A friend and companion never meet wrongfully; 
But above both is a wife with her husband.
40.24:
Brothers are a help for time of trouble; 
But kind deeds shall deliver more than them both.
40.25:
Gold and silver make a solid footing; 
But counsel is esteemed above them both.
40.26:
Wealth and power lift the heart; 
But the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is above them both. 
There is no lack with the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And with it you need not seek help.
40.27:
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is a garden of beraḵah, 
And covers him above all esteem.
40.28:
My son, do not lead a beggar’s life; 
For better it is to die than to beg.
40.30:
Begging is sweet in the mouth of the shameless; 
But in his inward parts a fire burns.

41.2:
O death, your lot is acceptable to the needy, 
And to him whose strength fails, that is now in the last age, and pained with all, 
And to he who despairs, and has lost patience!
41.4:
And why are you against the decision of the Most High? 
There is no searching in the grave, 
Whether you have lived ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years.
41.5:
The children of sinners are abominable children, 
And those who keep company in the dwelling of the wicked.
41.6:
The inheritance of the children of sinners shall perish, 
And their descendants shall be an everlasting reproach.
41.7:
The children complain of a wicked father, 
Because they shall be reproached for his sake.
41.8:
Woe unto you, wicked men, who have forsaken the Law of the Most High Elohim! 
For if you increase, it shall be to your destruction:
41.9:
And if you are born, you shall be born into a curse: 
And if you die, a curse shall be your lot.
41.10:
All that are of the earth shall turn to earth again; 
So the wicked shall go from a curse to destruction.
41.11:
The mourning of men is over their bodies; 
But the evil name of sinners shall be blotted out.
41.12:
Have regard for your name; 
For that shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold.
41.13:
A good life has few days; 
But a good name endures forever.
41.15: A man that hides his foolishness is better than a man that hides his wisdom.
41.17:
Be ashamed of whoring before your father and mother; 
And of a lie before a prince and a mighty man;
41.20:
And of silence before those who greet you; 
And to look upon a whore;
41.23:
Or of repeating and speaking again that which you have heard; 
And of revealing of secrets.
41.24: So you shall be truly ashamed and find favor before all men.

42.1: Of these matters do not be ashamed, and allow no one to sin by them:
42.2:
Of the Law of the Most High, and His Covenant; 
And of judgment to declare the wicked right;
42.3:
Of reckoning with your partners and travelers; 
Or of the gift of the inheritance of friends;
42.4:
Of exactness of balance and weights; 
Or of acquiring much or little;
42.6:
Where a wicked wife is, safe- keeping is good; 
And shut up, where many hands are.
42.7:
Deliver all by number and weight; 
And put in writing all that you give out, or receive in.
42.11:
Keep a close watch over a shameless daughter, 
Lest she make you a laughing-stock to your enemies, 
And a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people, 
And make you ashamed before the assembly.
42.12:
Do not look upon the loveliness of every woman, 
And do not sit in the midst of women.
42.13: For a moth comes from garments, and wickedness from women.
42.14:
Better is the hardness of a man than a courteous woman, 
A woman who brings shame and reproach.
42.15:
I shall now remember the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and declare that which I have seen: 
In the Words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are His works, 
And all His creation does His desire.
42.16:
The sun that gives light looks upon all, 
And its doing is full of the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
42.17:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not given power to the qodeshim to declare all of His marvelous works, 
Which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty firmly settled, 
That whatever exists might be established for His esteem.
42.19:
He declares matters that are past, and those to come, 
And reveals the path of that which is hidden.
42.20:
No thought escapes Him, 
Nor is any word hidden from Him.
42.21:
He has adorned the excellent works of His wisdom, 
And He is from everlasting to everlasting: 
Unto Him none is added, nor shall He be diminished, 
And He has no need of any counsellor.
42.22:
Oh how desirable are all His works! 
And that a man may see even a spark.
42.23:
All these live and remain forever for all uses, 
And they are all obedient.
42.24:
All matters are equal, one against another; 
And He has made none imperfect.
42.25:
One establishes the good of another; 
And who is ever filled with looking upon His esteem?

43.1:
The pride of the heights, the clear expanse, 
The loveliness of the shamayim, with His esteemed display;
43.2:
The sun when it appears, showing a marvelous instrument at its rising; 
The work of the Most High.
43.3:
At noon it scorches the land, 
And who shall stand its burning heat?
43.5:
Great is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who made it; 
And at His command it runs speedily.
43.6:
He made the moon also to serve in its season for appointed times, 
And a sign for the world.
43.7:
From the moon is the sign of Feasts, 
A light that decreases in its completion.
43.9:
The loveliness of the shamayim, the esteem of the stars, 
An ornament giving light in the highest places of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
43.10:
At the command of the Qadosh One they stand in their order, 
And never weary in their watches.
43.11:
Look upon the rainbow, and baraḵ Him who made it; 
It is very lovely in its brightness.
43.12:
It surrounds the shamayim with a splendid arc, 
And the hands of the Most High have bent it.
43.13:
By His command He makes the snow to fall in place, 
And sends the lightnings of His judgment swiftly.
43.14:
Through this the storehouses are opened; 
And clouds fly onward as birds.
43.15:
By His great power He makes the clouds pour out, 
And the hailstones are broken small.
43.16:
At His sight the mountains are shaken, 
And at His desire the south wind blows.
43.17:
The noise of thunder causes the earth to tremble; 
So does the northern storm and the whirlwind. 
As birds flying He scatters the snow, 
And its falling is as the settling of grasshoppers.
43.18:
The eye marvels at the loveliness of its whiteness, 
And the heart is astonished at its falling.
43.19:
He also pours the frost as salt upon the earth, 
And being hardened, it lays on the top as sharp icicles.
43.20:
When the cold north wind blows, and the water is hardened into ice, 
It remains upon every collection of water, 
And clothes the water like a breastplate.
43.21:
It devours the mountains, and burns the wilderness, 
And consumes the grass like fire.
43.22:
A mist coming speedily stands as a healer of all, 
A refreshing dew coming after heat.
43.23:
By His counsel He calms the deep, 
And plants islands within it.
43.24:
Those who sail on the sea tell of its dangers; 
And when we hear it with our ears, we marvel at it.
43.25:
For in it are strange and wondrous works, 
Differing kinds of all creatures and whales created.
43.26:
By Him the end of them has a benefit of good, 
And by His word all exists.
43.27:
We may speak much, and yet come short; 
Therefore in summary, He is all.
43.28:
How are we able to exalt Him? 
For He is great above all His works.
43.29:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is awesome and exceedingly great, 
And His power is marvelous.
43.30:
When you esteem 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, exalt Him as much as you may; 
For He shall even yet far exceed. 
And when you exalt Him, deliver all your strength, 
And do not be weary; for you shall never declare enough.
43.31:
Who has seen Him, that he might tell us? 
And who could exalt Him as He is?
43.32:
There are still greater than these which are hidden, 
For we have seen but a few of His works.
43.33:
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has made all; 
And to the reverent has he given wisdom.

44.1:
Let us now praise men of name, 
And our fathers who brought us forth.
44.2:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has worked great esteem by them, 
Through His great power from the beginning.
44.3:
Those who ruled in their reigns, men named for their strength, 
Giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring neḇuoth.
44.5: Such who compose musical songs, and speak verses in writing;
44.6: Wealthy men equipped with resource, living peaceably in their dwellings;
44.7:
All these were esteemed in their generations, 
And were the esteem of their times.
44.8:
There are some of them who have left behind a name, 
That their praises might be declared.
44.10:
But these were kind men, 
Whose righteousness has not been forgotten.
44.11:
With their seed a good inheritance shall continually remain, 
And their children are within the Covenant.
44.12:
Their seed stands fast, 
And their children for their sakes.
44.13:
Their seed shall remain forever, 
And their esteem shall not be blotted out.
44.14:
Their bodies are buried in peace; 
But their name lives forever.
44.15:
The people shall tell of their wisdom, 
And the assembly shall declare their praise.
44.16:
Ḥanoḵ pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and was translated, 
Being an example of repentance to all generations.
44.18:
An everlasting Covenant was made with him, 
That no longer would all flesh perish by the flood.
44.19:
Aḇraham was a great father of many people; 
There was none like him in esteem;
44.21:
Therefore He assured him with an oath, 
That He would baraḵ the nations in his seed, 
And that He would multiply him as the dust of the earth, 
And exalt his seed as the stars, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea, 
And from the River unto the utmost part of the land.
44.22:
With Yitsḥaq He likewise established the beraḵah of all men, and the Covenant, 
And caused it to rest upon the head of Ya’aqoḇ. 
He acknowledged him with His bireḵoth, 
And gave him an inheritance, and divided his portions; 
Among the twelve tribes He divided them.

45.1:
And He brought out from him a kind man, who found favor in the sight of all flesh, 
Even Mosheh, beloved of Elohim and men, whose remembrance is held in bireḵoth.
45.2:
He made him like the esteemed qodeshim, 
And exalted him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.
45.3:
By his words He caused the wonders to cease, 
And He made him esteemed in the sight of melaḵim, 
And gave him a Command for His people, 
And showed him part of His esteem.
45.4:
He qadosh him in his trustworthiness and humility, 
And chose him out of all men.
45.5:
He caused him to hear His voice, and brought him into the thick cloud, 
And gave him Commands before His face, 
Even the Law of Ḥai and knowledge, 
That he might teach Ya’aqoḇ His Covenant, 
And Yisra’ĕl his Right-Rulings.
45.6:
He exalted Aharon, a qodesh man like him, 
Even his brother, of the tribe of Lĕwi.
45.7:
He made an everlasting Covenant with him, 
And gave him the kehunnah among the people; 
He adorned him with comely ornaments, 
And clothed him with a robe of esteem.
45.9:
And He surrounded it with pomegranates, 
And with many golden bells all around, 
So that as he walked there would be a sound, 
And a noise made that would be heard in the Hĕyḵal, 
For a remembrance to the children of His people;
45.11:
With woven scarlet, the work of the skilled workman, 
With precious stones engraved like seals, and mounted in gold, 
The work of the engraver with writing engraved for a remembrance, 
After the number of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl.
45.12:
He placed a crown of gold upon the turban, in which was engraved QODESHAH, 
An ornament of esteem, a precious work, 
The desire of the eyes, elegant and lovely.
45.13:
Before him there were none like them, 
Nor did any stranger ever put them on, 
But only his children and his children’s children for all time.
45.14: Their offerings shall be completely consumed twice every day continually.
45.15:
Mosheh ordained him, and anointed him with qodesh oil: 
This was appointed to him with an everlasting Covenant, 
And to his seed, so long as the shamayim should remain, 
That they should serve Him, and execute the office of the kehunnah, 
And baraḵ the people in His Name.
45.16:
He chose him out of all men living to offer slaughterings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Incense, and a sweet savor, for a remembrance, 
To make atonement for His people.
45.17:
He gave him His Commands, and authority in the Laws of Right-Rulings, 
That he should teach Ya’aqoḇ the Witnesses, 
And instruct Yisra’ĕl in His Torot.
45.18:
Foreigners conspired together against him, 
And scorned him in the wilderness, 
Even the men that were on the side of Dathan and Aḇiram, 
And the assembly of Qoraḥ, with rage and wrath.
45.21:
For they eat of the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Which He gave to him and his seed.
45.23:
The third in esteem is Pineḥas the son of Eli’ezer, 
Because he had ardor in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, 
And made atonement for Yisra’ĕl.
45.26:
Elohim give you wisdom in your heart to rightly-rule His people in righteousness, 
That their good is not abolished, and that their esteem may endure forever.

46.1:
Yahoshua the son a Nun was a brave warrior, 
And was the successor of Mosheh in neḇuoth, 
Who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of Elohim, 
And taking vengeance on the enemies that rose up against them, 
That he might place Yisra’ĕl in their inheritance.
46.2:
What great esteem he attained, when he lifted up his hands, 
And stretched out his sword against the cities!
46.3:
Who before him ever stood up to it? 
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Himself brought his enemies to him.
46.4:
Did the sun not go back by His doing? 
And was not one day as long as two?
46.5:
He called upon the Most High Ĕl, when the enemies pressed upon him on every side; 
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty heard him.
46.6:
And with hailstones of great strength He made the battle fall violently against the nations, 
And at the descent he destroyed those who resisted, 
That the nations might know all their strength, 
Because he fought in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And he followed the Almighty.
46.7:
In the time of Mosheh he also did a work of kindness, 
He and Kalĕḇ the son of Yephunneh, 
In that they withstood the assembly, 
And withheld the people from sin, and appeased the wicked murmuring.
46.8:
And of six hundred thousand people on foot, 
These two were preserved to bring them into the inheritance, 
Even to the land that flows with milk and honey.
46.10: That all the children of Yisra’ĕl might see that it is good to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
46.11:
And concerning the judges, every one by name, 
Whose heart did not go whoring, nor departed from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Let their memory be held in bireḵoth.
46.12:
Let their bones flourish from their place, 
And let the name of those who were esteemed be continued upon their children.
46.13:
Shemu’ĕl, the naḇi of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, beloved of his Aḏon, 
Established a reign, and anointed princes over His people.
46.14:
By the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 he rightly- ruled the assembly, 
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 showed respect toward Ya’aqoḇ.
46.15:
By his trustworthiness he was found a true naḇi, 
And by his word he was known to be trustworthy in vision.
46.16:
He called upon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty, 
When his enemies pressed upon him on every side, 
When he offered the suckling lamb.
46.17:
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 thundered from the shamayim, 
And with a great noise made His voice heard.
46.18:
And He destroyed the rulers of the people of Tsor, 
And all the princes of the Pelishtites.
46.19:
And before his long sleep he bore witness in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and His anointed, 
“I have not taken any man’s goods, so much as a shoe.” 
And no man accused him.
46.20:
And after his death he naḇa, and showed the meleḵ his end, 
And lifted up his voice from the earth in neḇuah, 
To blot out the wickedness of the people.

47.1: And after him rose up Nathan to naḇa in the time of Dawiḏ.
47.2:
As the fat is taken away from the peace offering, 
So Dawiḏ was chosen out of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
47.3:
He played with lions as with young goats, 
And bears as with lambs.
47.4:
Did he not slay a giant, when he was still young? 
And did he not take away the reproach of the people, 
When he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, 
And beat down the boasting of Golyath?
47.6:
So the people esteemed him with ten thousands, 
And praised him with the bireḵoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
In that He gave him a crown of esteem.
47.7:
For he destroyed their enemies on every side, 
And brought to naught his adversaries, the Pelishtites, 
And broke their horn in pieces to this day.
47.9:
He also appointed singers before the altar, 
That with their voices they made sweet melody, 
And sang praises daily with their songs.
47.10:
He adorned their Feasts, and put in order the Appointed Times until the end, 
That they should praise His qodesh Name, 
And that the Hĕyḵal might resound from the morning.
47.11:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 took away his sins, and exalted his horn forever: 
He gave him a Covenant of melaḵim, 
And a throne of esteem in Yisra’ĕl.
47.12: After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake his dwelling was broad.
47.13:
Shelomoh reigned in a peaceable time, and was esteemed; 
For Elohim made quiet all around him, 
That he might build a House for His Name, 
And prepare His Miqdash forever.
47.14:
How wise you were in your youth, 
And filled with understanding as a flood!
47.15: Your being covered the whole earth, and you filled it with deep parables.
47.16:
Your name went to the far islands; 
And for your peace you were loved.
47.17: The lands marveled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.
47.18:
By the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, which is called 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, 
You gathered gold as tin and multiplied silver as lead.
47.19:
You bowed your loins to women, 
And by your body you were brought into subjection.
47.21: So the reign was divided, and out of Ephrayim ruled a rebellious reign.
47.22:
But the kindness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall never cease, 
Nor shall any of His works perish, 
Neither shall He cut off the descendants of His elect, 
And the seed of he who loves Him He shall not take away; 
Therefore He gave a remnant to Ya’aqoḇ, 
And out of him, a root of Dawiḏ.
47.23:
Thus Shelomoh rested with his fathers, 
And of his seed he left behind him Reḥaḇ’am, 
Even the foolishness of the people, and one who had no understanding, 
Who turned the people away through his counsel. 
There was also Yaroḇ’am the son of Neḇat, 
Who caused Yisra’ĕl to sin, and showed Ephrayim the way of sin;
47.24:
And their sins were multiplied exceedingly, 
So they were driven out of the land.
47.25:
For they sought out all wickedness, 
Till the punishment came upon them.

48.1:
Then Ĕliyahu the naḇi stood up as fire, 
And his word burned like a lamp.
48.2:
He brought a severe scarcity of food upon them, 
And by his ardor he diminished their number.
48.3:
By the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 he shut up the shamayim, 
And also brought down fire three times.
48.4:
O Ĕliyahu, how you were esteemed in your wondrous deeds! 
And whose esteem is like yours?
48.6:
Who brought melaḵim to destruction, 
And honorable men from their bed;
48.7:
Who heard the rebuke of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Sinai, 
And the judgment of punishment in Ḥorĕḇ;
48.8:
Who anointed melaḵim to take vengeance, 
And neḇi’im to succeed after him;
48.9:
Who was taken up in a whirlwind of fire, 
And in a chariot of fiery horses;
48.10:
Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, 
To appease the wrath of judgment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Before it broke forth into wrath, 
And to turn the heart of the father to the son, 
And to restore the tribes of Ya’aqoḇ.
48.11:
Ashrĕ are those who saw You, and slept in love; 
For we shall surely live.
48.12:
It was Ĕliyahu who was covered with a whirlwind; 
And Elisha was filled with His Ruaḥ. 
While he lived, he was not moved by the presence of any prince, 
Nor could any bring him into subjection.
48.13:
No word could overcome him; 
And after his death his being naḇa.
48.14:
He did wonders in his life, 
And at his death his works were marvelous.
48.16:
Of whom some did that which was pleasing to Elohim, 
And some multiplied sins.
48.18:
In his time Sanḥĕriḇ came up, and sent the Raḇshaqĕh, 
And lifted up his hand against Tsiyon, 
And boasted proudly.
48.19:
Then their hearts and hands trembled, 
And they were in pain, as women in childbirth.
48.20:
But they called upon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is kind, 
And stretched out their hands toward Him. 
And immediately the Qadosh One heard them out of the shamayim, 
And delivered them by the service of Yeshayahu.
48.21:
He smote the army of Ashshur, 
And His messenger destroyed them.
48.22:
For Ḥizqiyahu had done that which pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And was strong in the Ways of Dawiḏ his father, 
As Yeshayahu the naḇi, who was great and trustworthy in his vision, had commanded him.
48.23:
In his time the sun went backward, 
And he lengthened the meleḵ’s life.
48.24:
He saw by an excellent spirit what would come to pass, 
And he comforted those who mourned in Tsiyon.
48.25:
He showed what should come to be at the end of time, 
And secrets before they came to be.

49.2:
He acted uprightly by instructing the people, 
And took away the wicked abominations.
49.3:
He directed his heart toward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And in the time of the wicked he established the worship of Elohim.
49.5:
Therefore He gave their strength to others, 
And their esteem to a foreign nation.
49.6:
They burned the chosen city of the Miqdash, 
And made the streets desolate, 
According to the neḇuah of Yirmeyahu.
49.8:
It was Yeḥezqĕl who saw the esteemed vision, 
Which was shown to him upon the chariot of the keruḇim.
49.9:
For he remembered the enemies under the sign of rain, 
And directed those who went rightly.
49.11:
How shall we exalt Zerubbaḇel? 
Even he was as a signet on the right hand;
49.12:
So was Yĕshua son of Yotsaḏaq; 
Who in their time built the House, 
And raised a qodesh Hĕyḵal to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
Which was prepared for everlasting esteem.
49.13:
And among the elect was Neḥemyah, 
Whose name is great, who raised up for us the walls that had fallen, 
And put up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again.
49.14:
But no man on the earth was created like Ḥanoḵ; 
For he was taken from the earth.
49.15:
Neither was there a young man born like Yosĕph, 
A governor over his brothers, a support to the people, 
Whose bones were regarded by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
49.16:
Shĕm and Shĕth were in great esteem among men, 
And so was Aḏam above every living creature in creation.

5.1:
Do not lay your heart upon your goods; 
And do not say, “I have enough for my life.”
5.2:
Do not follow your own mind and strength, 
To walk in the ways of your heart:
5.3:
And do not say, “Who shall control me in my deeds?” 
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall surely punish your pride.
5.4:
Do not say, “I have sinned, and what harm has befallen me? 
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is patient, He shall by no means let you go.
5.5:
Concerning atonement, 
Do not be without reverence to add sin unto sin;
5.6:
And do not say, “His kindness is great; 
He shall be appeased for the multitude of my sins.” 
For kindness and wrath come from Him, 
And His wrath rests upon sinners.
5.7:
Do not delay to turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and do not put off from day to day; 
For suddenly the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall come forth, 
And in your security you shall be destroyed, 
And perish in the day of vengeance.
5.8:
Do not lay your heart upon goods acquired unrighteously, 
For they shall not profit you in the day of calamity.
5.9:
Do not winnow with every wind, and do not go into every way: 
For so does the sinner that has a double tongue.
5.10:
Be steadfast in your understanding; 
And let your word be the same.
5.11:
Be swift to hear; and let your being be sincere; 
And give answer with patience.
5.12:
If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; 
If not, put your hand over your mouth.
5.13:
Esteem and shame is in speech; 
And the tongue of man is his downfall.
5.14:
Do not be a whisperer, and do not lie in wait with your tongue; 
For foul shame is upon the thief, and an evil condemnation upon the double-tongued.
5.15: Do not be ignorant of any matter, great or a small.

50.2:
And by him the double height from the foundation was built, 
The high fortress of the wall around the Hĕyḵal;
50.3:
In his days the cistern to receive water, being surrounded as the sea, 
Was covered with plates of bronze;
50.4:
He looked after of the Hĕyḵal that it should not fall, 
And fortified the city against a siege.
50.5:
How esteemed he was in the midst of the people, 
When coming out of the Miqdash!
50.6:
He was as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, 
And as the moon in its fullness;
50.7:
As the sun shining upon the Hĕyḵal of the Most High, 
And as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds,
50.9:
As fire and incense in the fire holder, 
And as a vessel of beaten gold mounted with all kinds of precious stones;
50.10:
And as a fair olive tree budding forth fruit, 
And as a cypress which grows up to the clouds.
50.11:
When he put on the robe of esteem, 
And was clothed with the perfection of esteem, 
When he went up to the qodesh altar, 
He made the garment of qodeshah esteemed.
50.12:
When he took the portion out of the hands of the kohenim, 
He himself stood by the hearth of the altar, 
Surrounded as a young cedar in Leḇanon; 
And as palm trees they surrounded him.
50.13:
So were all the sons of Aharon in their esteem, 
And the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in their hands, 
Before all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl.
50.14:
And finishing the service at the altar, 
That he might adorn the offering of the Most High Almighty,
50.15:
He stretched out his hand to the cup, 
And pouring the blood of the grape, 
He poured out at the foot of the altar, 
A sweet fragrance to the Most High Meleḵ of all.
50.16:
Then the sons of Aharon shouted, 
And sounded the silver trumpets, 
And made a great noise to be heard, 
For a remembrance before the Most High.
50.17:
Then all the people hurried together, 
And fell down on their faces on the earth to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Ĕl Shaddai, the Most High.
50.18:
The singers also sang praises with their voices, 
With all kinds of sounds sweet melody was made.
50.19:
And the people sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Most High, 
By prayer before He who is kind, 
Till the qodeshah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had ended, 
And they had finished His service.
50.20:
Then he went down, and raised his hands over the whole assembly of the children of Yisra’ĕl, 
To give the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with his lips, and to rejoice in His Name.
50.21:
And they bowed themselves down to worship a second time, 
That they might receive a beraḵah from the Most High.
50.22:
Now therefore baraḵ the Elohim of all, 
Who does only wondrously everywhere, 
Who exalts our days from the womb, 
And deals with us according to His kindness.
50.23:
He gives joy to the heart, 
And that peace may be in our days in Yisra’ĕl forever;
50.24:
That He would confirm His kindness with us, 
And deliver us in His time!
50.25:
There are two manner of nations which my heart abhors, 
And the third is no nation:
50.26:
Those who sit on the mountain of Shomeron, 
And those who dwell among the Pelishtites, 
And those foolish people who dwell in Sheḵem.
50.27:
Yahoshua the son of Sira of Yerushalayim, 
Has written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, 
From whose heart poured out wisdom.
50.28:
Ashrĕ is he who shall be exercised in these; 
And he who treasures them up in his heart shall become wise.
50.29:
For if he does them, he shall be strong in all; 
For the light of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 leads he who gives wisdom to the reverent. 
Baruḵ be the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 forever. 
Amĕn, Amĕn.

51.2:
For You are my Defender and Helper, 
And have preserved my body from destruction, 
And from the snare of the slanderous tongue, 
And from the lips that forge lies, 
And have been my Helper against my adversaries;
51.3:
And have delivered me, according to the multitude of Your kindnesses and greatness of Your Name, 
From the teeth of those who were ready to devour me, 
And out of the hands of those who sought after my life, 
And from the great afflictions which I had;
51.4:
From the choking fire on every side, 
And from the midst of the fire which I did not kindle;
51.5:
From the depth of the inward parts of She’ol, 
From an unclean tongue, and from lying words.
51.6:
By an accusation to the meleḵ from an unrighteous tongue, 
My being drew near unto death, 
My life was near to She’ol beneath.
51.7:
They surrounded me on every side, 
And there was no one to help me. 
I looked for the support of men, but there was none.
51.8:
Then I thought upon Your favor, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And upon Your acts of old, 
How You save those who wait on You, 
And save them out of the hands of their enemies.
51.9:
Then I lifted up my supplications from the earth, 
And prayed for deliverance from death,
51.10:
I called upon Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Father, 
That He would not leave me in the days of my trouble, 
And in the time of the proud, when there was no help.
51.12:
For You saved me from destruction, 
And delivered me from the evil time; 
Therefore I thank and praise You, 
And baraḵ Your Name, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!
51.13:
When I was still young, or if I ever went travelling, 
I desired wisdom openly in my prayer.
51.14:
I prayed for her before the Hĕyḵal, 
And shall seek her to the end.
51.15:
Even from the flower till the grape was ripe, 
My heart has delighted in her; 
My foot went the right way, 
From my youth upward I sought after her.
51.16:
I bowed down my ear a little, and received her, 
And acquired much learning.
51.17: I profited in this, therefore I shall ascribe esteem to He who gives me wisdom.
51.19:
My being has wrestled with her, 
And in my doings I was exact. 
I stretched forth my hands to the shamayim above, 
And bewailed my ignorance’s of her.
51.20:
I directed my being unto her, 
And I found her in pureness. 
I have had my heart joined with her from the beginning, 
Therefore I shall not be forsaken.
51.21:
My heart was troubled in seeking her; 
Therefore I have received a good possession.
51.22:
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given me a tongue for my reward, 
And I shall praise Him with it!
51.23:
Draw near unto me, you unlearned, 
And dwell in the house of learning.
51.24:
Why are you slow, and what do you say to these? 
Seeing your beings are very thirsty.
51.25:
I opened my mouth, and said, 
“Acquire her for yourselves without silver.”
51.26:
Put your neck under the yoke, and let your being receive instruction; 
She is found to be close at hand.
51.27:
See with your eyes, how I have only little labor, 
And have received much rest.
51.28:
Acquire learning with a great sum of silver, 
And get much gold by her.
51.29:
Let your being rejoice in His kindness, 
And do not be ashamed of His praise.
51.30:
Work your work early, 
And in His time He shall give you your reward.

6.2:
Do not exalt yourself in the counsel of your own heart; 
That your being be not torn in pieces as a bull.
6.3:
You shall consume your leaves, and lose your fruit, 
And leave yourself as a dry tree.
6.4:
A wicked being shall destroy he who possesses, 
And shall cause him to be laughed to scorn by his enemies.
6.5:
Sweet words shall multiply friends, 
And a favorable tongue shall increase kind greetings.
6.6:
Be at peace with many; 
But have just one counsellor in a thousand.
6.7: If you would get a friend, prove him first and do not be hasty to trust him.
6.8:
For a certain man is a friend for his own occasion, 
And shall not remain in the day of your trouble.
6.9: And there is a friend, who being turned to enmity, shall cause strife and uncover your reproach.
6.10:
Again, there is a friend, a companion at the table, 
But shall not continue in the day of your affliction.
6.11:
When you are prosperous he shall be as you are, 
And shall be bold over your servants.
6.12:
If you are brought low, he shall be against you, 
And shall hide himself from your face.
6.13:
Separate yourself from your enemies, 
And be on guard with your friends.
6.14:
A trustworthy friend is a strong defense; 
And he who has found such a one has found a treasure.
6.15:
There is none that makes up for a trustworthy friend, 
And his worth is invaluable.
6.16:
A trustworthy friend is the healing of life; 
And those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall find Him.
6.17:
Whoever reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 directs his friendship well; 
For as he is, so shall his neighbor be also.
6.18:
My son, gather instruction from your youth onward; 
So you shall gain wisdom till your old age.
6.20:
She is very unpleasant to the unlearned; 
He who is without understanding shall not remain with her.
6.21:
She shall lay upon him as a mighty stone of trial; 
And he shall throw her from him before long.
6.22:
For wisdom is according to her name, 
And she is not revealed to many.
6.23:
Listen my son, receive my advice, 
And do not refuse my counsel,
6.24:
And put your feet into her shackles, 
And your neck into her chain.
6.25:
Bow down your shoulder, and bear her, 
And do not be grieved with her bonds.
6.26:
Come to her with your whole heart, 
And guard her ways with all your strength.
6.27:
Search and seek, and she shall be made known unto you; 
And when you have taken hold of her, do not let her go.
6.28:
For in the end you shall find her rest, 
And that shall turn out for your joy.
6.29:
Then her shackles shall be a strong defense for you, 
And her chains a robe of esteem.
6.30:
For there is a golden ornament upon her, 
And her bands are purple lace.
6.31:
You shall put her on as a robe of esteem, 
And shall lay her upon you as a crown of joy.
6.32:
My son, if you allow, you shall be taught; 
And if you apply your mind, you shall be clever.
6.33:
If you love to listen, you shall receive understanding; 
And if you bow your ear, you shall be wise,
6.34:
Stand in the group of the elders; 
And cling to he who is wise.
6.35:
Be willing to hear every worthy discourse; 
And do not let the parables of understanding escape you.
6.36:
And if you see a man of understanding, 
Get yourself to him early, 
And let your feet wear out his doorstep.

7.1: Do no evil, so no harm shall come to you.
7.2: Depart from the unrighteous, and evil shall turn away from you.
7.3:
My son, do not sow upon the furrows of unrighteousness, 
And you shall not reap them sevenfold.
7.4: Do not seek superiority from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Neither of the royal seat of esteem.
7.5:
Do not declare yourself right before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; 
And do not boast of your wisdom before the meleḵ.
7.7:
Do not cause the crowd of a city to stumble, 
And then you shall not be brought low among the people.
7.8:
Do not bind one sin upon another; 
For not one shall go unpunished.
7.9:
Do not say, “Elohim shall look upon the multitude of my offerings, 
And when I offer to the Most High Elohim, He shall accept it.”
7.10:
Do not be faint-hearted when you make your prayer, 
And do not neglect to give in kindness.
7.11:
Mock no man in the bitterness of his being; 
For there is One who humbles and exalts.
7.12:
Do not plan a lie against your brother; 
Neither do likewise to your friend.
7.13:
Refuse to make any manner of lie; 
For the way of this is not good.
7.14:
Do not use many words among a multitude of elders, 
And do not make much babbling when you pray.
7.15:
Do not hate laborious work, neither work of the land, 
Which the Most High has ordained.
7.16:
Do not number yourself among the crowd of sinners, 
But remember that wrath shall not delay.
7.17:
Humble yourself greatly; 
For the punishment of the wicked is fire and worms.
7.18:
Do not exchange a friend for goods by any means; 
Neither a trustworthy brother for the gold of Ophir.
7.19:
Do not forsake a wise and good woman; 
For her favor is above gold.
7.20:
When your servant works trustworthily, do not mistreat him. 
Nor the hired man that gives himself completely for you.
7.21: Let your being love a good servant, and do not withhold his freedom.
7.22:
Do you have cattle? Keep an eye on them; 
And if they are for your profit, keep them with you.
7.23:
Do you have children? Instruct them, 
And bow their neck from their youth.
7.24:
Do you have daughters? 
Look after their body, 
And do not be too generous toward them.
7.25:
Give your daughter in marriage, and you shall have performed a weighty matter; 
But give her to a man of understanding.
7.27:
Esteem your father with your whole heart, 
And do not forget the sorrows of your mother.
7.28:
Remember that you were brought forth by them; 
And how would you repay them what they have done for you?
7.29: Revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all your being, and revere His kohenim.
7.30:
Love He who made you with all your strength, 
And do not forsake his servants.
7.32:
And stretch out your hand to the poor, 
That your beraḵah may be perfected.
7.33:
A gift has favor in the sight of every living man; 
And do not hold back for the dead.
7.34:
Do not fail to accompany those who weep, 
And mourn with those who mourn.
7.35:
Do not be slow to visit the sick; 
For that shall cause you to be loved.
7.36:
Whatever you take in hand, remember the end, 
And you shall never do wrong.

8.1: Do not strive with a mighty man lest you fall into his hands.
8.2:
Do not quarrel with a wealthy man, lest he outweigh you; 
For gold has destroyed many, and twisted the hearts of melaḵim.
8.3:
Do not strive with a man that is a babbler, 
And do not heap wood upon his fire.
8.4:
Do not jest with a rude man, 
Lest your ancestors be shamed.
8.5:
Do not reproach a man that turns from sin, 
But remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
8.6:
Do not shame a man in his old age; 
For even some of us grow old.
8.7:
Do not rejoice over the death of your greatest enemy, 
But remember that we all die.
8.8:
Do not despise the discourse of the wise, 
But acquaint yourself with their proverbs; 
For from them you shall learn instruction, 
And how to serve great men with ease.
8.9:
Do not avoid the discourse of the elders; 
For they also learned from their fathers, 
And from them you shall learn understanding, 
And to give answer as needed.
8.10:
Do not kindle the coals of a sinner, 
Lest you be burned with the flame of his fire.
8.11:
Do not rise up at the presence of an insuiter, 
Lest he lie in wait to entrap you in your words.
8.12:
Do not lend to he who is mightier than yourself; 
For if you lend to him, count it but lost.
8.13:
Do not be guarantor above your ability; 
For if you be guarantor, take care to pay it.
8.14:
Do not go to law against a judge; 
For they shall judge for him according to his esteem.
8.15:
Do not travel on the way with one who is headstrong, 
Lest he become burdensome to you; 
For he shall do according to his own desire, 
And you shall perish with him through his folly.
8.16:
Do not strive with a man of wrath, 
And do not go with him to a lonely place; 
For bloodshed is naught in his sight, 
And where there is no help, he shall overthrow you.
8.17:
Do not counsel a fool; 
For he does not heed advice.
8.18:
Do not speak secrets before a stranger; 
For you do not know what he shall reveal.
8.19:
Do not open your heart to every man, 
Lest he repay you craftily.

9.1:
Do not be jealous over the wife of your bosom, 
And do not teach her an evil lesson against yourself.
9.2: Do not give yourself to a woman to trample your strength.
9.3: Do not go into a whore, lest you fall into her snares.
9.4:
Do not keep company with a flirtatious woman, 
Lest you be taken by her attempts.
9.5:
Do not stare upon a maiden, 
So you do not fall by that which is precious in her.
9.6:
Do not give yourself to whores, 
So that you do not lose your inheritance.
9.7:
Do not look about in the streets of the city, 
Neither wander in its lonely places.
9.9:
Do not sit at all with another man’s wife, 
Nor sit down with her in your arms, 
And do not spend your silver with her on wine; 
Lest your heart incline toward her, 
And so, through your desire fall into destruction.
9.11:
Do not envy the esteem of a sinner; 
For you do not know what his end shall be.
9.12:
Do not delight in that which the wicked have pleasure in; 
But remember they shall not go unpunished to their grave.
9.13:
Keep far from the man who has power to kill; 
So the fear of death shall not concern you. 
And if you encounter him, make no mistake, 
Lest he take away your life immediately. 
Remember that you walk in the midst of snares, 
And that you walk upon the walls of the city.
9.14:
When you draw near, reason with your neighbor, 
And consult with the wise.
9.15:
Let your words be with the wise, 
And all your talk in the Law of the Most High.
9.16:
And let righteous men eat and drink with you; 
And let your esteem be in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
9.17:
For the hand of the craftsman the work shall be praised, 
And the wise ruler of the people for his words.
9.18:
A man of an evil tongue is dangerous in his city; 
And he who is hasty with his words shall be hated.
